A graph $G=(V,E)$ with a given independent set $S\subseteq V$ (a set of pairwise non-adjacent vertices) is said to be a chain partitioned probe graph if $G$ can be extended to a chain graph by adding edges between certain vertices in $S$. %there exists a set $E'\subseteq\binom{S}{2}$ such that the graph $G'=(V,E\cup E')$ is a chain graph. In this note we give two characterizations for chain partitioned probe graphs. The first one describes chain partitioned probe graphs by six forbidden subgraphs. The second one characterizes these graphs via a certain ``enhanced graph'': $G$ is a chain partitioned probe graph if and only if the enhanced graph $G^*$ is a chain graph. This is analogous to a result on interval (respectively, chordal, threshold, trivially perfect) partitioned probe graphs, and gives an $O(m^2)$-time recognition algorithm for chain partitioned probe graphs.
item.dc:creator: Van Bang Le

item.title: Gaps for PLRS with zero coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.23991v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Zeckendorf proved that every positive integer has a unique decomposition as a sum of non-adjacent Fibonacci numbers. Among its extensions, we focus on Positive Linear Recurrence Sequences (PLRS): fixed depth recurrences with non-negative integral coefficients whose first and last terms are positive: $G_{n+1} = c_1 G_n + \dots + c_L G_{n-L+1}$ with $c_i$ non-negative integers and $c_1 c_L \ge 1$. We again find every integer can be written uniquely as an appropriate sum of terms of the sequence, and we can study the distribution of gaps between summands in decompositions. Bower et al. (2015) proved that if each $c_i \ge 1$ then the distribution of gaps in the generalized Zeckendorf decompositions of integers in $[G_n, G_{n+1})$ converges to a geometric decay for gaps at least two. What if some of the $c_i$'s are allowed to be zero? To date only the Kangaroo case, where there is a fixed $g$ such that $c_i = 1$ if $i \equiv 1 \bmod g$ and 0 otherwise, has been done and again geometric behavior emerges. Ben-Ari and Miller (2016) developed a probabilistic framework that also produce similar results, but their approach requires more advanced machinery. One of the goals of this paper is to show that the elementary methods used by Bower et al. (2015) can be adapted to this setting as well. We analyze the case $H_{n+1} = H_n + H_{n-p} + H_{n-p-q}$. For gaps at least $\max(p,q)$ we again prove geometric decay, with parameter the largest root of the characteristic polynomial associated with the recurrence. For the finitely many smaller gaps, under the restriction $p<q+2$, we prove that the limiting probabilities exist and can be computed using a transfer-matrix method, yielding results that depend on $p,q,$ and the gap size $g$. The case $p \ge q+2$ is not addressed by our small-gap argument.
item.dc:creator: Yinxi Chen, Zongyun Chen, Brian Hii, Steven J. Miller

item.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in $\mathbb{F}_2^7$
item.description: arXiv:2610.24022v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a nonempty subset of the binary vector space $\mathbb{F}_2^7$ is spectral if and only if it tiles $\mathbb{F}_2^7$ by translations. This is the smallest binary dimension left open by Ferguson and Sothanaphan. For the implication from tiling to spectrality we show that every eight-point subset of $\mathbb{F}_2^d$ admits $2^{d-3}$ frequencies whose pairwise differences avoid the zeros of its Fourier transform; consequently every tile of $\mathbb{F}_2^d$ with at least $2^{d-3}$ elements is spectral. For the converse implication, we use the Smith normal form of the Walsh matrix to exclude every spectral subset of $\mathbb{F}_2^7$, and of $\mathbb{F}_2^8$, whose size is not a power of two. The sizes $16$ and $32$ are reduced, by a projection argument, to the tiling of point sets attached to binary log-Hadamard matrices of small rank. Using the published classifications of Hadamard matrices of orders $16$ and $32$, we find that exactly sixteen order-$32$ classes up to transposition have dephased binary rank at most seven, and we give explicit tilings for both orientations of each.
item.dc:creator: Atsushi Kadowaki

item.title: Sumsets regularity versus Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity for monomial curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.24121v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $A=\{0=a_0<a_1<\dots<a_{k-1}=d\}$ be integers with greatest common divisor $1$, let $C_A$ be the projective monomial curve they define, and let $\mathrm{reg}(A)$ be the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of its coordinate ring. Gimenez and Gonz\'alez-S\'anchez proved $\mathrm{reg}(A)\le\sigma(A)+1$ for the sumsets regularity $\sigma(A)$; the reverse inequality $\sigma(A)\le\mathrm{reg}(A)$ was proposed as an open conjecture in a 2024 talk. We show that it fails and measure by how much. Let $c_1,c_2$ be the conductors of the two numerical semigroups attached to $A$ and $N=\lceil(c_1+c_2)/d\rceil$. For curves in $\mathbb{P}^3$ that are not arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay, $\mathrm{reg}(A)\ge(c_1+c_2)/d+2$, with equality exactly for the arithmetically Buchsbaum curves, and $\sigma(A)=\mathrm{reg}(A)$. For arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay curves in $\mathbb{P}^3$ we prove $9N\le10\,\mathrm{reg}(A)-2$, with $9/10$ best possible, and give an explicit family with $\sigma(A)-\mathrm{reg}(A)$ unbounded. In $\mathbb{P}^4$ a family with a band-shaped Ap\'ery set has $\mathrm{reg}(A)/\sigma(A)\to(2+\sqrt2)/4$ along the solutions of a Pell equation, and gluing carries this bound to every $\mathbb{P}^r$ with $r\ge5$.
item.dc:creator: Prashant Chaudhary, Kapil Khandelwal

item.title: T-embeddings as stationary measures on T-graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.24180v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the relation between t-embeddings and T-graphs associated with the same weighted planar bipartite graph. We prove that, given such a T-graph, the corresponding t-embeddings are classified by positive stationary measures on this T-graph and describe a reconstruction procedure of the t-embedding given such a measure. As an application, we develop an approach for constructing t-embeddings of arbitrary sufficiently non-degenerate planar bipartite graphs.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail Basok, Benoit Laslier, Marianna Russkikh

item.title: Sums of two dependent uniform random variables: a characterization by joint tail bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.24197v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Which laws can the sum of two uniform random variables have when nothing is known about how they depend on each other? For three or more uniform summands, convex order gives the answer; for two it does not, and the question has been open. We show that the attainable laws are exactly those that satisfy a family of explicit joint bounds on sums of tail probabilities, one bound for each finite set of thresholds. For laws with a density at most one, convex order alone decides. For densities at most two, convex order implies the simplest of the joint bounds, and the constant two cannot be raised for single-threshold bounds. The number of thresholds a law needs is set by the spacing of its atoms, not by how many atoms it has.
item.dc:creator: Prashant Chaudhary, Kapil Khandelwal

item.title: Bounded powers of edge ideals: Nearly Gorenstein polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.24438v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A lattice polytope $\mathcal{P} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ of dimension $n$ is called nearly Gorenstein if $\mathcal{P}$ is normal and if its Ehrhart ring is a nearly Gorenstein ring. We study nearly Gorenstein polytopes arising from discrete polymatroids of bounded powers of edge ideals. Especially, it is shown that every nearly Gorenstein polytope coming from either a complete graph or a complete bipartite graph is level.
item.dc:creator: Takayuki Hibi, Seyed Amin Seyed Fakhari

item.title: On the $\omega$-circular $*$-distribution for complex unimodular $\omega$
item.description: arXiv:2610.24443v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider a notion of $\omega$-circular $*$-distribution $\mu_{\omega}$, defined in terms of a parameter $\omega \in \mathbb{C}$ with $| \omega |=1$. This $*$-distribution appears as limit law in an algebraic central limit theorem (CLT) for $\omega$-commuting unitaries, and interpolates between the Fermionic setting (at $\omega = -1$) and the Bosonic one (at $\omega = 1$). On a combinatorial level, $\mu_{\omega}$ is described in terms of pair-partitions of sets $\{1, ... ,2n\}$, where one has a total order among the $n$ pairs of the partition and where every pair is assigned a direction, to the effect that one can define the sign of a crossing between two pairs. The main goal of the paper is to study a significant subspace, with "Fock space" flavour, of the $L^2$-space associated to a natural multi-variate version of $\mu_{\omega}$. The inner product on this subspace is defined by a sesquilinear form $\langle \cdot \, , \, \cdot \rangle_{\omega}$ on non-commutative polynomials. We explicitly describe $\langle \cdot \, , \, \cdot \rangle_{\omega}$ in terms of some tractable non-negative definite functions on symmetric groups, and we prove that it is non-degenerate if and only if $\omega$ is not a root of unity.
item.dc:creator: Claus Koestler, Liam McQuay, Alexandru Nica

item.title: Avoiding Distances
item.description: arXiv:2610.24803v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a finite planar point set $X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}$, let $a_1<a_2< \cdots < a_s$ denote the $s \leq {n \choose 2}$ different (Euclidean) distances between points in $X$. The aim is to retain as many of the points as possible such that certain imposed inter-pair distances are avoided. For example, we show that: (A) Given a set $X$ of $n$ points in the plane, an independent set of size $0.2293 n$ in the unit distance graph determined by $X$ can be found in $O(n^2)$ time. For any fixed $k \in \mathbf{N}$ there exists a constant $c_k>0$ such that for any set $X$ of $n$ points in the plane, and set $D$ of size $k$, there exists a subset $X' \subseteq X$ of size $|X'| \geq c_k |X|$ in which no pair of points is at some distance in $D$ (we say that $X'$ avoids distances in $D$). Such a set can be found efficiently. (B) (i) There is a subset of $X$ of size $n/2$ that avoids the maximum distance; this bound cannot be improved. (ii) There is a subset of $X$ of size $8n/47$ that avoids both the minimum and maximum distance; on the other hand, there exists $X$ such that at most $5n/16$ points can be retained with this property. (iii) There is a subset of $X$ of size $n/7$ whose diameter is at most half the original diameter; on the other hand, there exists $X$ such that at most $n/6$ points can be retained with this property. (C) (i) For any $\varepsilon>0$, a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation for \textsc{MIS} in the minimum distance graph of $n$ points in the plane can be found in $2^{O(1/\varepsilon)} n^{O(1)}$ time. (ii) Given a set $X$ of $n$ points in the plane, a maximum independent set in the graph of diameters can be computed in $O(n^2)$ time. The techniques used to handle the planar case can be extended to $\mathbf{R}^d$ for any fixed dimension $d$.
item.dc:creator: Adrian Dumitrescu, Zsolt L\'angi

item.title: The locally quaternion group is a countable $B$-group
item.description: arXiv:2610.25022v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A group $G$ is a $B$-group if every primitive permutation group containing a regular subgroup isomorphic to $G$ is doubly transitive. We prove that the locally quaternion group $\mathrm{Dic}(C_{2^\infty},c)$, the extension of the Pr\"ufer $2$-group by an element squaring to its involution and inverting it, is a $B$-group. This gives an example of a countably infinite $B$-group. This answers Problem 13.30 of the Kourovka Notebook. The proof analyses the automorphism group of an orbital Cayley graph through the central involution. In the main case two half-flip automorphisms generate, with their conjugates, an elementary abelian normal subgroup whose orbits form a nontrivial block system; in the remaining case, where the pointwise stabilizers of the two cosets of the Pr\"ufer group have order two, the conjugates of the central translation generate an elementary abelian normal subgroup, which would be regular if the automorphism group were primitive; an affine lemma for the Pr\"ufer group excludes this. The proof does not depend on computer verification: its two finite case analyses are written out in full, and programs that re-check them are provided as ancillary files.
item.dc:creator: Alex J. Sutherland

item.title: Lambda number of the reduced power graph of finite groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.25028v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The reduced power graph $\Gamma_{RP}(G)$ of a group $G$ is a simple graph with vertex set $G$, where two distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent if and only if $\langle u \rangle \subset \langle v \rangle$ or $\langle v \rangle \subset \langle u \rangle$. An $L(2,1)$-labeling of a graph $\Gamma$ is a mapping from the vertex set of $\Gamma$ to the set of non-negative integers such that the labels of adjacent vertices differ by at least $2$ and the labels of vertices at distance two are distinct. The lambda number of $\Gamma$, denoted by $\lambda(\Gamma)$, is defined as the minimum possible span of labels among all $L(2,1)$-labelings of $\Gamma$. In this paper, we establish upper and lower bounds for $\lambda(\Gamma_{RP}(G))$ and characterize the conditions under which these bounds are achieved. As an application, we determine the exact value of $\lambda(\Gamma_{RP}(G))$ for certain classes of finite groups.
item.dc:creator: Siddharth Malviy, Keerttiranjan Sahoo, Vipul Kakkar

item.title: A characterization of finite modular 2-groups via magnitude homology
item.description: arXiv:2610.25030v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Finite quasihamiltonian groups - that is, finite groups in which every pair of subgroups commutes - admit several characterizations. In this work, after introducing the notion of sectional contractibility graph, we provide a new characterization in terms of (a suitable subgroup of) magnitude homology. Our approach especially focuses on the subgroup lattices of finite groups and on the related notion of modularity. We present a detailed study for finite 2-groups, and, in particular, in the case of extraspecial 2-groups and Pauli groups. These groups, of interest because of their diverse applications in both mathematics and physics, already describe the wealth of information that one can obtain in restricting the study to the case of 2-groups.
item.dc:creator: Luigi Caputi, Francesco G. Russo

item.title: Approximating Independent Sets Using Additive Combinatorics
item.description: arXiv:2610.25047v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a deterministic quasi-polynomial time algorithm for approximating the largest independent set in a graph. We show that if an $N$-vertex graph contains an independent set of size $2^{-t} N$, then we can find an independent set of size $2^t$ in quasi-polynomial time, for all $t$ up to a constant factor of $(\log N)^{1/3}$. This gives an approximation factor of $N / \exp((\log N)^{1/3})$, which has the same shape as known hardness results for quasi-polynomial time algorithms, up to a different exponent of the logarithm. The algorithm builds on a structural principle: a graph containing a large independent set must also contain a large sparse structured set, and such a set can be found efficiently. A greedy algorithm then extracts an independent set from it. Our proof draws on tools in additive combinatorics, in particular spreadness and sifting, to obtain the combinatorial structural results. We then convert these to efficient algorithms using pseudo-marginals obtained by semidefinite programming.
item.dc:creator: Shachar Lovett

item.title: When Are Monomial Symmetric Polynomials Hard?
item.description: arXiv:2610.25181v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a partition $\boldsymbol{\lambda} = (\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r)$ and $n\ge r$, the monomial symmetric polynomial is defined as $$m_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}(x_1,\ldots,x_n) := \sum x_{i_1}^{\lambda_1} x_{i_2}^{\lambda_2} \cdots x_{i_r}^{\lambda_r},$$ where the sum ranges over all distinct monomials obtained by assigning the parts of $\boldsymbol{\lambda}$ to pairwise distinct variables. We establish an almost-complete dichotomy for the complexity of the monomial symmetric polynomials $m_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}$: If a family of partitions contains polynomially many distinct parts, then the corresponding monomial symmetric polynomials (on sufficiently many variables) are VNP-complete. If the number of distinct parts is constant, the family admits polynomial-size circuits. Thus the only remaining gap concerns the intermediate regime where the number of distinct parts grows subpolynomially. As part of our proof, we use combinatorial properties of matching polynomials to establish VNP-hardness of the perfect matching polynomial for blow-up graphs; these are graphs with non-generic edge-weights that are obtained by "blowing up" a smaller graph. We reduce these matching polynomials to monomial-symmetric polynomials by combining classical techniques from algebraic complexity theory with structural properties of Sidon sets.
item.dc:creator: Markus Bl\"aser, Radu Curticapean, Sagnik Dutta, Gorav Jindal

item.title: On simplicial maps with non-zero Hopf invariant
item.description: arXiv:2610.25562v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In general, it is interesting to investigate the complexity of simplicial maps under various topological constraints. In this paper, we consider maps between (triangulated oriented rational homology) manifolds with non-zero Hopf invariant and establish bounds on the simplicial complexity of the fiber of a regular point. The lower bound, which is cubic in the dimension, is proved via a refinement of a theorem of S. Eilenberg. The upper bound is notable in that it is uniform with respect to the Hopf invariant.
item.dc:creator: Sergei Vad. Fomin

item.title: Two Generalizations of the G_0 Dichotomy
item.description: arXiv:2610.25587v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give classical proofs of the generalizations of the $\mathbb{G}_0$ dichotomy to $\kappa$-Souslin digraphs and uniformly analytic sequences of digraphs indexed by $\kappa^{\mathbb{N}}$.
item.dc:creator: B. Miller

item.title: On solutions to tropical Monge-Amp\`ere equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.25602v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper develops convex analysis on tropical varieties and investigates the properties of the tropical Monge-Amp\`ere equations. We start by introducing notions of plurisubharmonic functions and K\"ahler forms on arbitrary tropical varieties. We show that many classical results of pluripotential theory extend to this setting, including an analogue of Demailly's regularization theorem. Next, we study the solutions to the tropical Monge-Amp\`ere equations. While we establish their uniqueness, we show that the existence is not guaranteed in general. More precisely, we prove that the tropical analogue of the Calabi-Yau theorem fails for any pair $(X, \theta)$ consisting of a compact tropical variety $X$ of dimension at least two satisfying a mild genericity assumption, and a tropical K\"ahler form $\theta$ on $X$. In particular, there exist measures compactly supported in the open part of $X$ that admit no solution. In contrast, for tropical varieties that are regular in codimension one, we show the existence of solutions. Finally, via strongly faithful tropicalizations whose existence is established in this paper, we relate the tropical solutions, when they exist, to the solutions of non-Archimedean Monge-Amp\`ere equations on Berkovich spaces.
item.dc:creator: Omid Amini, Matthieu Piquerez, Lyuhui Wu

item.title: Big Ramsey degrees and structures in relational languages
item.description: arXiv:2610.25715v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a precompact transfer theorem for big Ramsey structures and a uniform envelope theorem for valuation hypergraphs. These yield big Ramsey structures for generic injective relational structures in languages with finitely many symbols of each positive arity, answering the existence part of Problem 6.3.2 of Balko et al. (arXiv:2110.08409), and refute Conjecture 4.7 of Braunfeld et al. (arXiv:2301.13116). We also construct a finitely constrained free amalgamation class in a finite language of maximum arity three whose Fra\"iss\'e limit has infinite singleton big Ramsey degree, giving a negative answer to the existence question in Problem 6.3.3 of Balko et al.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Hu

item.title: Terao's freeness conjecture for arrangements of 15 and 16 lines
item.description: arXiv:2610.25868v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that Terao's freeness conjecture holds for arrangements of 15 and of 16 lines in the complex projective plane. Together with the theorem of Barakat and K\"uhne for at most 14 hyperplanes, this shows that freeness of a central arrangement of at most 16 planes in $\mathbb{C}^3$ is determined by its intersection lattice. The proof has a theoretical and a computational part. Combining published combinatorial criteria for freeness (due to Abe, Dimca, Dimca-K\"uhne-Pokora and Yoshinaga) with Bojanowski's Hirzebruch-type inequality and an elementary counting identity, we show that a counterexample would have exponents $(6,8)$ or $(7,7)$ for 15 lines and $(7,8)$ for 16 lines, and an intersection lattice subject to strong numerical constraints. We then enumerate all 22,544,280 simple rank 3 matroids satisfying these constraints, up to isomorphism, and determine the complex realization space of each of them exactly over $\mathbb{Q}$. Exactly eleven of them are realizable over $\mathbb{C}$, and on each of these the freeness of the realizations is constant. As a by-product we classify the free arrangements of 15 and 16 lines that are not divisionally free, have maximal multiplicity smaller than the smaller nontrivial exponent, and have at least four intersection points on every line.
item.dc:creator: Cristian Anghel, Rare\c{s} Stan

item.title: New Maximum Hermitian $d$-Codes and New Invariants from Skew Polynomial Rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.26048v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Maximum rank-distance codes were introduced independently by Delsarte (1978) and Gabidulin (1985) for unrestricted matrix spaces, and their study was subsequently extended to the classical form spaces of alternating, symmetric, and Hermitian matrices. For Hermitian $d$-codes, Schmidt (2018) established the upper bound and constructed optimal additive codes for all admissible parameters except when $n$ and $d$ are both even and $4\le d\le n-2$. We settle this final open existence case, more generally, construct additive maximum Hermitian rank-metric codes for every admissible length and minimum distance. Rather than working directly in the space of Hermitian matrices, we construct our objects within central simple algebras with unitary involution arising from quotients of skew polynomial rings. We also introduce scalar-field and Lyapunov operators in these algebras, leading to new invariants for the equivalence of additive Hermitian codes. Explicitly determining these invariants yields strong necessary conditions for Hermitian equivalence and demonstrates that our construction contains a large number of pairwise inequivalent codes.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Santonastaso, Yue Zhou

item.title: The rank of the random $k$-XORSAT matrix beyond satisfiability
item.description: arXiv:2610.26300v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The random $k$-XORSAT matrix is an $m\times n$ random matrix $\mathbf A$ over $\mathbb F_2$ that represents a random instance of the $k$-XORSAT problem. Each row of $\mathbf A$ contains precisely $k\geq3$ non-zero entries in random positions. The rows are drawn independently. The matrix $\mathbf A$ is known to have full row rank for $m/n$ below the random $k$-XORSAT satisfiability threshold, which is known explicitly [Dubois, Mandler~2002; Pittel, Sorkin~2016]. Motivated by a problem from quantum game theory and refining a result of Cooper, Frieze and Pegden (2019), we determine the limiting distribution of the rank of $\mathbf A$ beyond the satisfiability threshold.
item.dc:creator: Amin Coja-Oghlan, Maurice Rolvien

item.title: Decomposing the Action of Macdonald Operators for Classical Types
item.description: arXiv:2610.26389v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Macdonald operators associated to classical root systems of types $B_N$, $C_N$, and $D_N$. We provide explicit formulas for decomposing the cumulative action of these operators as the sum of the actions of lower-rank operators and auxiliary operators. We also discuss the same idea in the elliptic case, also known as Ruijsenaars operators, and show that under the trigonometric limit, the identity reduces to type-$A_N$ decomposition.
item.dc:creator: Hieu Trung Vu

item.title: Exact cost of the Euclidean Maximum Traveling Salesman Problem in one dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.26536v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the random Euclidean Maximum Traveling Salesman Problem: finding a Hamiltonian cycle of maximal total cost through any set of $N$ cities on a line, where each edge cost is a function of its Euclidean length. We characterize the maximizing cycles for convex increasing, concave increasing, and convex decreasing cost functions. For points sampled independently and uniformly from the unit interval, we derive explicit expressions for the average maximal cost for arbitrary $N$ and asymptotic expansions with power-law edge costs.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Caracciolo, Carlo Vanoni

item.title: Geodesics in the continuous Hecke monoid
item.description: arXiv:2610.26700v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A permuton is a probability measure on the unit square with uniform marginals, the limit shape of a sequence of permutations. The sticky product of permutons is a continuous analogue of the Demazure product in the $0$-Hecke monoid; on copulas, the distribution functions of permutons, it is given by the tropical $(\min,+)$ product $\odot$. We show that every absolutely continuous rotation-invariant probability measure $\rho$ on the plane, which we call the profile, generates a one-parameter family of copulas $C^\rho=\{C^\rho_\beta\}_{\beta\in[0,\pi]}$. A copula in this family is defined by a pair of projections of a $\rho$-distributed random vector onto directions at angle $\pi-\beta$. Along this family, the sticky product adds angles: $$C^\rho_{\beta_1}\odot C^\rho_{\beta_2}=C^\rho_{\min(\beta_1+\beta_2,\pi)}.$$ Hence every non-identity element of such a family is a sticky product of two others and has roots of every natural degree. The normalized inversion number of the copula $C^\rho_\beta$ equals $\beta/\pi$. For the Archimedean measure $\mathfrak{Arch}$ the family $C^{\mathfrak{Arch}}$ consists of the limit shapes of the permutations of the uniformly random sorting network, found by Angel et al. and Dauvergne. For the Gaussian measure $\mathcal{N}$ the family $C^{\mathcal{N}}$ consists of Gaussian copulas and contains $\mathit{Unif}$, the uniform measure on the square (the limit shape of the uniformly random permutation); its square root within this family is the Gaussian copula with correlation $-1/\sqrt2$. By the Herschel-Maxwell theorem the Gaussian measure is the only profile whose family contains $\mathit{Unif}$; nevertheless, $\mathit{Unif}$ has another, singular, sticky square root. A discrete analogue of the Gaussian family is the geometric sorting network generated by rotating independent Gaussian points: after rotation by $\pi/2$ its permutation is exactly uniform.
item.dc:creator: Sergei Presniakov, Alexander Tiskin

item.title: The sum-product conjecture holds for fixed-field lattice product constructions
item.description: arXiv:2610.26737v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study fixed-field analogues of the lattice product construction recently used by Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, and Zhelezov to disprove the sum-product conjecture over the real numbers. These sets are of the form $A_n = P_nG_n \subset F$, where $F$ is a fixed number field, $P_n$ can be rescaled to a set of algebraic integers whose conjugates are polynomially bounded in $|P_n \setminus \{0\}|$, and $G_n$ occupies a positive proportion of a bounded box of scale $Y_n$ in a fixed positive-rank multiplicative lattice. We prove that these fixed-field constructions satisfy the sum-product conjecture, $\max\{|A_n+A_n|, |A_nA_n|\} \ge |A_n|^{2-o(1)}$ as $|A_n| \to \infty$, with no restriction on the relative growth of the two factors. More strongly, any fixed power saving in the product set forces an asymptotically maximal sumset: there exists $C > 0$ such that, for each fixed $\delta \in (0,1]$, if $|A_nA_n| \le |A_n|^{2-\delta}$ for all sufficiently large $n$, then $Y_n \to \infty$ and $|A_n+A_n|/|A_n|^2 = 1/2 + O_\delta((\log Y_n)^C/Y_n)$. In particular, the additive-box times unit-box construction of Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, and Zhelezov cannot produce sum-product counterexamples in any fixed totally real number field, at any relative scales. The proof combines a bound for factorizations of algebraic integers with a more general maximal-sumset theorem for coefficient sets whose nonzero-element ratios have small Weil height. The latter controls multiplication fibers and combines a lattice strip estimate with logarithmic separation derived from the theorems of Yu and Matveev.
item.dc:creator: Harrison Lemley, David Chew

item.title: Weights of KZ motives and quantum groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.26774v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov (KZ) connection is defined on the constant bundle determined by $n$ finite-dimensional irreducible representations of a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and a nonzero complex parameter $\kappa$, over the configuration space of $n$ distinct points on the affine line. Work of Schechtman--Varchenko and Looijenga shows that, when $\kappa$ is rational, the resulting local systems admit natural motivic realizations, called KZ motives. The Kazhdan--Lusztig equivalence identifies the local systems underlying these motivic variations with certain representations of the pure braid group arising from the corresponding Lusztig quantum group at a root of unity. We formulate conjectures relating the weight filtrations of KZ motives to structures in quantum-group representation theory, particularly tilting modules and the Jantzen and Andersen filtrations, and provide evidence for these conjectures. Our methods use a new deformation of the representation ring that records the first moments of the weight filtration, together with Schmid's theorem on limiting mixed Hodge structures and results on the Hodge filtration obtained in earlier joint work with S. Mukhopadhyay.
item.dc:creator: Prakash Belkale, Najmuddin Fakhruddin

item.title: A simplified proof of the FPRAS for counting perfect matchings
item.description: arXiv:2610.26803v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a simplified, self-contained proof of OpenAI's FPRAS for counting perfect matchings in general graphs. As in the original proof, we use a restricted Poincar\'e inequality for two matchings to sample weighted perfect matchings and estimate their total weight. We simplify the proof of this inequality by isolating parts of alternating cycles directly on the original vertex set and controlling the resulting error terms. This avoids the auxiliary vertices and tree constructions used in the original proof. The argument preserves the required parameter bounds and yields the same FPRAS guarantee.
item.dc:creator: Chenghua Liu, Boning Meng

item.title: James reduced product schemes and double quasisymmetric functions
item.description: arXiv:2304.11508v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Symmetric function theory is a key ingredient in the Schubert calculus of Grassmannians. Quasisymmetric functions are analogues that are similarly central to algebraic combinatorics, but for which the associated geometry is poorly developed. Baker and Richter (2008) showed that $\operatorname{QSym}$ manifests topologically as the cohomology ring of the loop suspension of infinite projective space or equivalently of its combinatorial homotopy model, the James reduced product $J\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^\infty$. In recent work, we used this viewpoint to develop topologically-motivated bases of $\operatorname{QSym}$ and initiate a Schubert calculus for $J\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^\infty$ in both cohomology and $K$-theory. Here, we study the torus-equivariant cohomology of $J\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^\infty$. We identify a cellular basis and introduce double monomial quasisymmetric functions as combinatorial representatives, analogous to the factorial Schur functions and double Schubert polynomials of classical Schubert calculus. We also provide a combinatorial Littlewood--Richardson-type rule for the structure coefficients of this basis. Furthermore, we introduce an algebro-geometric analogue of the James reduced product construction. In particular, we prove that the James reduced product of a complex (quasi-)projective variety also carries the structure of a (quasi-)projective variety.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Pechenik, Matthew Satriano

item.title: On the Girth of Graph Lifts
item.description: arXiv:2401.01238v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The order of the smallest $k$-regular graph of girth at least $g$ is denoted by the well-studied function $n(k,g)$. We introduce an analogous function $n(H,g)$, defined as the smallest order of a graph of girth at least $g$ that is a lift (or cover) of the, possibly non-regular, graph $H$. We prove that the two main combinatorial bounds on $n(k,g)$, the Moore lower bound and the Erd\H{o}s-Sachs upper bound, carry over to the new lift setting. We also consider two other functions: i) The smallest order of a graph of girth at least $g$ sharing a universal cover with $H$. We prove that it is the same as $n(H,g)$ up to a multiplicative constant. ii) The smallest order of a graph of girth at least $g$ with a prescribed degree distribution. We discuss this known generalization and argue that the new suggested definitions are superior. We conclude with the best-known upper and lower bounds for covers of the diamond graph ($K_4 - e$) for girth up to $30$, obtained via a computerized search, and offer conjectures and open problems for future research.
item.dc:creator: Shlomo Hoory

item.title: Two Erdos-Hajnal-type theorems for forbidden order-size pairs
item.description: arXiv:2406.04154v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The celebrated Erd\H{o}s-Hajnal conjecture says that any graph without a fixed induced subgraph $H$ contains a very large homogeneous set. A direct analog of this conjecture is not true for hypergraphs. In this paper we present two natural variants of this problem which do hold for hypergraphs. We show that for every $r \geq 3$, $m \geq m_0(r)$ and $0 \leq f \leq \binom{m}{r}$, if an $r$-graph $G$ does not contain $m$ vertices spanning exactly $f$ edges, then $G$ contains much larger homogeneous sets than what is guaranteed to exist in general $r$-graphs. We also prove that if a $3$-graph $G$ does not contain homogeneous sets of polynomial size, then for every $m \geq 3$ there are $\Omega(m^3)$ values of $f$ such that $G$ contains $m$ vertices spanning exactly $f$ edges. This makes progress on a problem of Axenovich, Brada\v{c}, Gishboliner, Mubayi and Weber.
item.dc:creator: Fabian Arnold, Lior Gishboliner, Benny Sudakov

item.title: Backbone coloring for graphs with degree 4
item.description: arXiv:2409.10201v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $\lambda$-backbone coloring of the graph $G$ with backbone $H$ is a graph-coloring problem in which we are given a graph $G$ and a subgraph $H$, and we want to assign colors to vertices in such a way that the endpoints of every edge from $G$ have different colors, and the endpoints of every edge from $H$ are assigned colors which differ by at least $\lambda$. In this paper we pursue research on backbone coloring of bounded-degree graphs with well-known classes of backbones. Our result is an almost complete classification of the complexity of deciding whether $BBC_{\lambda}(G, H) \le k$ for graphs with maximum degree at most $4$ and matching, galaxy, Hamiltonian path, and spanning tree backbones. We also determine the effect of allowing isolated vertices in matching and galaxy backbones.
item.dc:creator: Krzysztof Michalik, Krzysztof Turowski

item.title: Notes on the Divisibility of Divisor Sums of Catalan Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2502.04619v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate divisibility questions for the sum-of-divisors function $\sigma(C_n)$ of the Catalan numbers $C_n=(n+1)^{-1}\binom{2n}{n}$. Using the prime factors occurring to exponent one in $C_n$, we give explicit divisors of $\sigma(C_n)$ and obtain, for each fixed integer $m\geq 2$, a power $m^{R_m(n)}$ dividing $\sigma(C_n)$, with $R_m(n)\sim\frac{2\log 2}{\varphi(m)}\frac{n}{\log n}$. We further prove uniform divisibility for all moduli up to fixed powers of $\log n$ and, with the same leading constant $2\log 2$, for almost all moduli up to $\sqrt{n}$ apart from logarithmic factors. We also establish a complete classification of the integers $m\geq 2$ for which $m\mid\sigma(mk-1)$ for every $k\geq 1$, identify precisely the exceptional coprimality relations among the associated linear forms, and record a twin-prime product divisor of $\sigma(C_n)$. The arguments use standard prime-distribution results and do not assume any conjecture concerning twin primes.
item.dc:creator: Volkan Yildiz

item.title: Hermitian adjacency matrices with at most three distinct eigenvalues
item.description: arXiv:2503.13781v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study oriented graphs whose Hermitian adjacency matrices of the second kind have few eigenvalues. We give a complete characterization of the oriented graphs with two distinct eigenvalues, showing that there are only four such graphs. We extend this result to mixed graphs. We show that there are infinitely many regular tournaments with three distinct eigenvalues. We extend our main results to Hermitian adjacency matrices defined over other roots of unity.
item.dc:creator: Saieed Akbari, Jonathan Aloni, Maxwell Levit, Bojan Mohar, Steven Xia

item.title: Unexpectedly, a symmetry on unlabeled graphs
item.description: arXiv:2505.03665v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We exhibit the joint symmetric distribution of the following two parameters on the set of unlabeled, simple, connected graphs with $n$ vertices. The first parameter is the maximal number of leaves attached to a vertex. The second parameter is the size of the largest set of vertices sharing the same closed neighborhood minus $1$. Apparently, this is the first example of a natural, non-trivial equidistribution of graph parameters on unlabeled connected graphs on a fixed set of vertices. Our proof is enumerative, using the theory of species. Exhibiting an explicit bijection interchanging the two parameters remains an open problem.
item.dc:creator: Florian F\"urnsinn, Moritz Gangl, Martin Rubey

item.title: Local Distance Antimagic Labeling of Neighborhood Balanced Colored Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2505.08134v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph without isolated vertices. A bijection $f\colon V\to \{1,2,\dots,|V|\}$ is called a local distance antimagic labeling if $w(u)\not=w(v)$ for every edge $uv\in E$, where the weight $w(u)$ of a vertex $u$ is defined as the sum of labels assigned to all vertices adjacent to $u$. The local distance antimagic chromatic number of $G$, denoted by $\chi_{ld}(G)$, is defined as the minimum number of colors taken over all colorings of $G$ induced by local distance antimagic labelings. In this paper, we investigate local distance antimagic labelings of the direct product and the union of certain classes of graphs, namely, neighborhood balanced $k$-colored graphs and nearly neighborhood balanced $k$-colored graphs.
item.dc:creator: Maurice Genevieva Almeida, Tarkeshwar Singh, Andrea Semanicova Fenovcikova

item.title: Cycle lengths in the percolated hypercube
item.description: arXiv:2506.16858v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $Q^d_p$ be the random subgraph of the $d$-dimensional binary hypercube obtained after edge-percolation with probability $p$. It was shown recently by the authors that, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, there is some $c = c(\varepsilon)>0$ such that, if $pd\ge c$, then typically $Q^d_p$ contains a cycle of length at least $(1-\varepsilon)2^d$. We strengthen this result to show that, under the same assumptions, typically $Q^d_p$ contains cycles of all even lengths between $4$ and $(1-\varepsilon)2^d$.
item.dc:creator: Michael Anastos, Sahar Diskin, Joshua Erde, Mihyun Kang, Michael Krivelevich, Lyuben Lichev

item.title: Solution to a problem on isolation of $3$-vertex paths
item.description: arXiv:2506.19149v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $3$-path isolation number of a connected $n$-vertex graph $G$, denoted by $\iota(G,P_3)$, is the size of a smallest subset $D$ of the vertex set of $G$ such that the closed neighbourhood $N[D]$ of $D$ intersects the vertex sets of the $3$-vertex paths of $G$, meaning that no two edges of $G-N[D]$ intersect. Zhang and Wu proved that $\iota(G,P_3) \leq 2n/7$ unless $G$ is a $3$-path or a $3$-cycle or a $6$-cycle. The bound is attained by infinitely many graphs having induced $6$-cycles. Huang, Zhang and Jin proved that if $G$ has no $6$-cycles, or $G$ has no induced $5$-cycles and no induced $6$-cycles, then $\iota(G, P_3) \leq n/4$ unless $G$ is a $3$-path or a $3$-cycle or a $7$-cycle or an $11$-cycle. They asked if the bound still holds asymptotically for connected graphs having no induced $6$-cycles. More precisely, taking $f(n)$ to be the maximum value of $\iota(G,P_3)$ over all connected $n$-vertex graphs $G$ having no induced $6$-cycles, their question is whether $\limsup_{n \to\infty}\frac{f(n)}{n} = \frac{1}{4}$. We verify this by proving that $f(n) = \left \lfloor (n+1)/4 \right \rfloor$. Therefore, induced $6$-cycles solely account for the jump to the bound $2n/7$. The proof hinges on further proving that if $G$ is such a graph and $\iota(G, P_3) = (n+1)/4$, then $\iota(G-v, P_3) < \iota(G, P_3)$ for each vertex $v$ of $G$. This new idea promises to be of further use. We also prove that if the maximum degree of such a graph $G$ is at least $5$, then $\iota(G,P_3) \leq n/4$.
item.dc:creator: Karl Bartolo, Peter Borg, Dayle Scicluna

item.title: Sign-coherence and tropical sign pattern for rank $3$ real cluster-cyclic exchange matrices
item.description: arXiv:2509.07454v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The sign-coherence about $c$-vectors was conjectured by Fomin-Zelevinsky and proved by Gross-Hacking-Keel-Kontsevich for integer skew-symmetrizable case. We prove this conjecture associated with $c$-vectors for rank 3 real cluster-cyclic skew-symmetrizable case. Simultaneously, we establish their self-contained recursion and monotonicity. Then, these $c$-vectors are proved to be roots of certain quadratic equations. Based on these results, we prove that the corresponding exchange graphs of $C$-pattern and $G$-pattern are $3$-regular trees. We also study the structure of tropical signs and equip the dihedral group $\mathrm{D}_6$ with a cluster realization via certain mutations.
item.dc:creator: Ryota Akagi, Zhichao Chen

item.title: Combinatorial Courant-Fischer-Weyl Minimax Principle on Cheeger $k$-constants of Weighted Forests
item.description: arXiv:2510.06301v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present several max-min and minimax characterizations of Cheeger $k$-constants in weighted forests, thereby providing the first combinatorial analogue of the Courant-\\Fischer-Weyl minimax principle. As for applications, we prove that the forest 1-Laplacian variational eigenvalues are independent of the choice of typical indexes; we propose a refined higher order Cheeger inequality which establishes a relationship between Miclo's multiway Cheeger constants and the variational eigenvalues of graph $p$-Laplacians; and we show a purely combinatorial proof for the equality $h_k=\lambda_k(\Delta_1)$ on trees which connects the 1-Laplacian variational eigenvalues and the multiway Cheeger constants.
item.dc:creator: Zijun Meng, Dong Zhang

item.title: The Homomorphism Submodule Graph
item.description: arXiv:2511.07837v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $M$ be a left $R$-module. We define the \emph{homomorphism submodule graph} $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Hom}}(M)$ as the simple graph whose vertices are the proper submodules of $M$, with an edge between distinct vertices $N_1$ and $N_2$ if and only if $\mathrm{Hom}_R(N_1, M/N_2) \ne 0$ or $\mathrm{Hom}_R(N_2, M/N_1) \ne 0$. This graph encodes homological information about $M$ and reflects its internal structure. We compute $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Hom}}(M)$ for semisimple and uniserial modules, establish precise correspondences between graph-theoretic and algebraic properties, and prove that for modules over Artinian local rings, the isomorphism type of $M$ is determined by $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Hom}}(M)$. We also show that over commutative rings with identity, the graph is always chordal, and we relate its spectral radius to composition length in natural families.
item.dc:creator: Shahram Mehry, Mansour Molaeinejad

item.title: Subexponential upper bound on the number of rich words
item.description: arXiv:2511.11069v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $R_q(n)$ denote the number of rich words of length $n$ over a fixed alphabet of size $q\geq2$. It is known that $R_q(n)^{1/n}\to1$. We establish a nonrecursive subexponential upper bound on the number of rich words, with its asymptotic growth quantified in terms of an iterated logarithm. For every $\lambda\in(1/2,1)$ and $\gamma>1$, there exists $c>0$ such that, for every positive function $\phi$ satisfying $\phi(n)\to\infty$ and $n/\phi(n)\to\infty$, the functions \[ f(n)=\left[c\ln^{*}\!\left(\frac{n}{\phi(n)}\ln q\right)\right]^{1/\gamma}, \qquad B(n)=q^{\frac{n}{\phi(n)}+\frac{n}{(2\lambda)^{f(n)-1}}} \] satisfy $R_q(n)\leq B(n)$ for all sufficiently large $n$ and $B(n)^{1/n}\to1$. Here $\ln^{*}$ is the iterated natural logarithm, with value zero on $(0,1]$. The proof iterates a counting inequality based on palindromic factorization and controls the resulting multiplicative constants using the iterated logarithm.
item.dc:creator: Josef Rukavicka

item.title: Graphical view on linear extensions of finite posets
item.description: arXiv:2511.11785v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: One of the possible cryptomorphic definitions of a partially ordered set (= a poset) $P$ on a non-empty finite ground set $N$ is in terms of the set ${\cal L}(P)$ of all its linear extensions, that is, in terms of the set of total orders on $N$ consistent with $P$. Any total order on $N$ can be interpreted as a node of a particular graph, called the permutohedral graph (over $N$), because it is indeed the graph of a certain polytope in $\mathbb{R}^{N}$, known as the permutohedron. It is shown in the paper that a non-empty set of total orders on $N$ equals to ${\cal L}(P)$ for some poset $P$ on $N$ if and only if it is a geodetically convex set in the permutohedral graph. This result means that a purely graphical concept of geodetical convexity in this graph is a cryptomorphic definition of a finite poset. In particular, the lattice of geodetically convex sets in this graph is graded and its height function is described in graphical terms. A counter-example, however, shows that the height function does not correspond to the usual graphical diameter, relating this matter to a combinatorial concept of the dimension of a poset. Two alternative cryptomorphic views on a poset $P$ on $N$ are also discussed. The geometric counterpart is its full-dimensional braid cone in $\mathbb{R}^{N}$, while a combinatorial alternative is a topology on $N$ distinguishing points, often referred as a (finite) distributive lattice.
item.dc:creator: Milan Studen\'y, V\'aclav Kratochv\'il

item.title: Directed Hamiltonicity in Generalized Kneser Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2511.12553v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the canonical orientation of the generalized Kneser graph $KG(n,k,s)$ contains a directed Hamiltonian cycle for all integers $s \geq 3$ and $n>sk$. Furthermore, we establish that the dichromatic number of this oriented graph is exactly $k$. As a special case, our results apply to the $s$-stable Kneser graphs $K_{s\text{-stab}}(n,k)$, resolving their directed Hamiltonicity and dichromatic number. Our proof adapts the class graph framework of Ledezma and Pastine to the directed setting, leveraging cyclic rotations and friend class adjacencies to construct a single directed cycle spanning all vertices. This work provides a unified and strengthened perspective on the Hamiltonian properties of Kneser-type graphs.
item.dc:creator: Shahram Mehry

item.title: Computing the Hopf invariant
item.description: arXiv:2512.03201v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider Whitehead's integral formula and propose an algorithm for computing the Hopf invariant for simplicial mappings.
item.dc:creator: Oleg R. Musin, Timur Shamazov

item.title: Universal polar dual pairs]{Universal polar dual pairs of spherical codes found in $E_8$ and the Leech lattice
item.description: arXiv:2512.25037v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We identify universal polar dual pairs of spherical codes $C$ and $D$ such that for a large class of potential functions $h$ the minima of the discrete $h$-potential of $C$ on the sphere occur at the points of $D$ and vice versa. Moreover, the minimal values of their normalized potentials are equal. These codes arise from the known hierarchies of sharp codes embedded in the even unimodular extremal lattices $E_8$ and $\Lambda_{24}$ (Leech lattice). This embedding allows us to use the lattices' properties to find new universal polar dual pairs. In the process we extensively utilize the interplay between the binary Golay codes and the Leech lattice. As a byproduct of our analysis, we identify a new universally optimal (in the sense of energy) code in the projective space $\mathbb{RP}^{21}$ with $1408$ points (lines). Furthermore, we extend the Delsarte-Goethals-Seidel definition of derived codes from their seminal $1977$ paper and generalize their Theorem 8.2 to show that if a $\tau$-design is enclosed in $k\leq \tau$ parallel hyperplanes, then each derived code is a $(\tau+1-k)$-design in the ambient subspace.
item.dc:creator: S. V. Borodachov, P. G. Boyvalenkov, P. D. Dragnev, D. P. Hardin, E. B. Saff, M. M. Stoyanova

item.title: Uniformity of extremal graph-codes
item.description: arXiv:2602.03298v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is an important fact that extremal discrete structures -- that is, discrete structures of maximal size among those that avoid certain configurations -- exhibit strong pseudorandom behavior. We present instances of this phenomenon in the context of \emph{graph-codes}, a notion put forth recently by Alon, as well as on problems related to the density polynomial Hales--Jewett conjecture.
item.dc:creator: No\'e de Rancourt, Pandelis Dodos, Konstantinos Tyros

item.title: Excluding an apex-forest or a fan as quickly as possible
item.description: arXiv:2602.03833v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that every graph $G$ excluding an apex-forest $H$ as a minor has layered pathwidth at most $|V(H)|-2$, and that every graph $G$ excluding an apex-linear forest (such as a fan) $H$ as a minor has layered treedepth at most $|V(H)|-2$. We further show that both bounds are optimal. These results improve on recent results of Hodor, La, Micek, and Rambaud (2025): The first result improves the previous best-known bound by a multiplicative factor of $2$, while the second strengthens a previous quadratic bound. In addition, we reduce from quadratic to linear the bound on the $S$-focused treedepth $\mathrm{td}(G,S)$ for graphs $G$ with a prescribed set of vertices $S$ excluding models of paths in which every branch set intersects $S$.
item.dc:creator: Quentin Claus, J\k{e}drzej Hodor, Gwena\"el Joret, Pat Morin

item.title: Computations on the tautological basis of the cohomology ring of the Peterson variety
item.description: arXiv:2602.14605v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is known that the set of square free monomials on the Chern classes of the tautological line bundles over the Peterson variety forms an additive basis of its cohomology ring. We study the expansion formula for their products. In particular, we give a square free expansion of the products multiplying degree 2 classes in terms of elementary symmetric polynomials and binomial coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Yuito Hashimoto

item.title: The record statistic and forward stability of Schubert products
item.description: arXiv:2604.02964v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We initiate a probabilistic study of forward stability for products of Schubert polynomials through the record statistic (left-to-right maxima) of permutations. Building on the explicit record formula for forward stability obtained by Hardt and Wallach, we study random pairs of permutations drawn from three natural families: uniform permutations, Grassmannian permutations, and Boolean permutations. For each family, we determine record probabilities and use them to analyze the asymptotic behavior of forward stability. For uniform and Grassmannian permutations, we obtain asymptotics for the mean together with limiting distribution results. For Boolean permutations, we prove linear-order growth of the mean, and our analysis also produces an explicit time-inhomogeneous Markov chain that yields an exact linear-time uniform sampler. Beyond these cases, we prove that the record-set statistic is equidistributed on the avoidance classes of $132$ and $231$, and consequently the corresponding forward stability distributions coincide. We conclude with conjectures for numerous further permutation classes and a conjectural recursive criterion for when two avoidance classes have the same record-set distribution.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Hardt, Reuven Hodges, Hanzhang Yin

item.title: Simultaneous avoidance of length-4 patterns in ascent sequences
item.description: arXiv:2604.06735v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Ascent sequences form a central class of combinatorial objects, as they are in bijection with several important families such as (2+2)-free posets, Stoimenow matchings, and other Fishburn objects, and are enumerated by the Fishburn numbers. We study pattern avoidance in ascent sequences for the five patterns of length 4: $0101$, $0102$, $0112$, $0120$, and $0121$. These patterns arise naturally from recent work on pattern avoidance in related families of Fishburn objects, including Stoimenow matchings and (2+2)-free posets. We enumerate ascent sequences avoiding any subset of these patterns, with the exception of the sets $\{0120\}$, $\{0121\}$, and $\{0120,0121\}$, for which the enumeration remains open. Our results reveal that the corresponding avoidance classes fall into $16$ Wilf equivalence classes and exhibit a wide range of enumerative behaviour, including connections to classical sequences such as the Catalan and Fibonacci numbers, as well as polynomial formulas and rational generating functions; several of the sequences we obtain appear to be new. Our methods combine structural decompositions with generating-tree techniques and, in several cases, rely on reductions to shorter patterns via restricted growth functions. This work contributes to the broader study of pattern avoidance across Fishburn families and highlights further connections between ascent sequences and other combinatorial structures.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Discrete Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science vol. 28:3 #18 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Qi Liu, Sergey Kitaev, Philip B. Zhang

item.title: A Weak Solution of Inverse Treblecross
item.description: arXiv:2604.16759v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Inverse Treblecross, the impartial avoidance version of the game Treblecross, in which completing a line of three X's is prohibited. We give a weak solution of the game: an empty board of $n$ cells is a $\mathscr{P}$-position (Sprague--Grundy value $0$) if and only if $n\equiv 0,2,3,6,9\pmod{10}$, and has value $1$ if $n\equiv 1,4,5,7,8\pmod{10}$. In particular the empty-board Sprague--Grundy sequence is the purely periodic sequence of period $10$ with values in $\{0,1\}$. The proof introduces two characteristic functions on $\mathbb Z/10\mathbb Z$ and a family of regular positions, and shows by induction that such a position splits, under a reduction move, into a disjunctive sum of regular positions whose sign product is preserved or inverted.
item.dc:creator: Kai Liang, Muxi Li

item.title: Cyclic Equalizability Characterized by Parikh Vectors
item.description: arXiv:2604.19504v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Cyclic equalizability is a notion introduced by Shinagawa and Nuida in 2025, in the study of card-based cryptography. Informally, a collection of words is cyclically equalizable if, by inserting the same letters at the same positions in all words, they can be transformed into words that are cyclic shifts of one another. Shinagawa and Nuida showed that two binary words of equal length are cyclically equalizable if and only if they have the same Hamming weight. They also posed the problem of characterizing cyclic equalizability over larger alphabets. In this paper, we completely characterize cyclic equalizability for two words over an arbitrary finite alphabet by proving that two words are cyclically equalizable if and only if they have the same Parikh vector.
item.dc:creator: Sarunyu Thongjarast, Sarit Pasiphol, Suthee Ruangwises

item.title: Optimization and complexity of inertia-type bounds on the independence and chromatic numbers of graph powers
item.description: arXiv:2605.00524v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The inertia bound, introduced by Cvetkovi\'c in 1971, is a fundamental result in spectral graph theory that provides an upper bound for the independence number of a graph in terms of spectral information about a weighted adjacency matrix of the graph. Recently, this bound has been extended to the so-called inertia-type bounds for estimating the independence and chromatic numbers of graph powers ($k$-independence number and distance-$k$ chromatic number of a graph). These bounds have recently found applications in coding theory and quantum information theory. The inertia-type bounds depend on the choice of a polynomial of degree $k$ and on the eigenvalues of the graph. Currently, optimizing these bounds requires solving several MILPs, which quickly becomes computationally demanding as the graph size or $k$ grows. This computational barrier is a major obstacle to the practical use of these bounds. Moreover, we have a limited theoretical understanding of their performance, even for small $k$. In this paper, we investigate their optimization and complexity. In particular, we improve the MILP formulations, reducing their computational burden and significantly decreasing the running time. Furthermore, we show that the optimization problems associated with the bounds are solvable in polynomial arithmetic time for every fixed $k$, given exact spectral input.
item.dc:creator: Aida Abiad, Stan van Hoesel, Valentin Michaux

item.title: $\boldsymbol{2}$-Neighbor Bootstrap Percolation on Odd Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2606.03687v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $r$-neighbor bootstrap percolation process on a graph $G$ is a vertex-activation process that begins with a set of initially active vertices. In each subsequent round, every inactive vertex having at least $r$ active neighbors becomes active. Denote by $m(G,r)$ the minimum number of initially active vertices whose activation eventually spreads to all vertices of $G$. Let \(\mathbbmsl{O}_k\) and \(\mathbbmsl{B}_k\) be the odd graph and the bipartite odd graph, respectively, both defined on a ground set of size \(2k+1\). In this article, among other results, we prove that $m(\mathbbmsl{O}_k, 2)=\lceil(k^2+3k+2)/4\rceil$ and $m(\mathbbmsl{B}_k, 2)=\lceil(k^2+2k+3)/2\rceil$. The former result confirms a conjecture posed in 2021 by Grippo, Pastine, Torres, Valencia-Pabon, and Vera.
item.dc:creator: Ali Mohammadian, Sina Rezaie Zareie, Behruz Tayfeh-Rezaie

item.title: On some structural properties of graphs with non-negative resistance curvature
item.description: arXiv:2607.13169v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A graph is called resistance nonnegative (RN), respectively resistance positive (RP), if it admits positive edge weights such that all vertex resistance curvatures are nonnegative, respectively positive. In this paper, we study the structure of RN and RP graphs in relation to toughness, traceability, and Cartesian products. First, we disprove a conjecture of Fiedler and answer a question of Devriendt in the negative by constructing, for every $n\ge 11$, an $n$-vertex $1$-tough graph that is not RN. Second, we show that RP graphs need not be traceable by proving that the Thomassen $34$-graph is RP but not traceable. Finally, we resolve a conjecture of Devriendt on grid graphs by proving that all Cartesian products of paths are RN.
item.dc:creator: Gyaneshwar Agrahari, Christin Bibby, Sean Boros, Hailey Jay Garcia, Fernando Heidercheidt, Zhiyu Wang

item.title: On the weight distribution bound for the negative eigenvalue of polar collinearity graphs
item.description: arXiv:2607.28153v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The weight distribution bound gives a lower bound on the weight of eigenvectors for eigenvalues of distance-regular graphs. In this note, we study when the weight distribution bound is tight for the negative eigenvalue of collinearity graphs of finite embedded polar spaces, and elliptic and hyperbolic affine polar graphs. We give a complete classification of eigenvectors meeting the weight distribution bound.
item.dc:creator: Sam Adriaensen, Jim Wittebol

item.title: Tight instances of the Lonely Runner Conjecture: one-entry modifications and the growth of speeds
item.description: arXiv:2608.13599v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a set $V$ of $n-1$ distinct positive integers let $\mathrm{LR}(V)=\max_{t}\min_{v\in V}\|vt\|$, where $\|x\|$ is the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. The Lonely Runner Conjecture asserts $\mathrm{LR}(V)\ge 1/n$, and $V$ is called tight if equality holds. Goddyn and Wong determined which of the sets obtained from $[n-1]=\{1,\dots,n-1\}$ by multiplying a single entry by an integer are tight. We complete the classification of arbitrary one-entry modifications $([n-1]\setminus\{r\})\cup\{w\}$, $w\ge n$: for $n\ge4$ such a set is tight if and only if it is of Goddyn--Wong type or is one of the two sporadic sets $\{1,3,4,7\}$ and $\{1,3,4,5,9\}$ found by Wills. The proof is elementary and rests on an exact description of the region left uncovered by the retained speeds. We then show that the largest speed $M(n)$ occurring in a tight one-entry modification satisfies $M(n)<0.60\,n\log n+52\,n$ and $\limsup_{n\to\infty}M(n)/(n\log n)=1/2$; in particular, tight sets are not confined to speeds $O(n)$. Along the way we give a short proof of Liu's closed formula for $\mathrm{LR}([n-1]\setminus\{2\})$ and show that $\mathrm{LR}([n-1]\setminus\{r\})>1/(n-1)$ for every $r\le n-2-2\sqrt n$, extending the range $r\le(n-1)/2$ covered by Liu's theorem. For two-entry modifications we show that no tight instance removes a speed $q$ with $2\le q\le n/10$ once $n\ge\max(40,10q)$, whatever the second removed speed and the inserted speeds are; an exact-arithmetic census for $8\le n\le140$ with inserted speeds at most $8n$ finds only two tight two-entry modifications, both already listed by Goddyn and Wong.
item.dc:creator: Yuhan Zhang

item.title: Recovering Laplacian Lattices from $L$-Functions of Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2608.29981v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce $L$-functions associated with characters of the Jacobian of a finite graph, as a graph-theoretic analogue of the $L$-functions arising from unramified coverings of algebraic curves. These $L$-functions are defined using the Riemann--Roch structure on the graph and extend Lorenzini's two-variable zeta function. We show that if two connected graphs without bridges have isomorphic Jacobians and their $L$-functions agree under the induced correspondence of characters, then their Laplacian lattices coincide. We also show that these $L$-functions satisfy a functional equation. Finally, we give examples showing that neither the Jacobian nor the Lorenzini zeta function alone determines the Laplacian lattice.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Labib, Antonio Lei

item.title: The Loopy Polynomial: from Tutte's Universal $V$-Function to Bizonotopal Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2609.07728v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the loopy polynomial L_G, a multivariate graph invariant arising from bizonotopal graphical algebras and defined by deletion and loopy contraction, in which the contracted edge is retained as a loop. It determines the Tutte polynomial and admits a spanning-forest expansion recording external activity componentwise. It also determines Stanley's chromatic symmetric function for every graph; the degree sequence, induced edge count profile, and independence polynomial for loopless graphs; and the clique and matching polynomials for simple graphs. Separating component size from external activity gives a refinement that is equivalent to the extended U-polynomial and the extended polychromate. The ordinary U-polynomial, Tutte's universal $V$-function, and Stanley's Tutte symmetric function are specializations of this refinement. We conjecture that L_G and U_G have the same distinguishing power on simple graphs, and verify this through eleven vertices. We exhibit five-vertex loopless multigraphs with equal U-polynomials but distinct loopy and extended U-polynomials, solving a problem of Merino and Noble. We also disprove Loebl's conjecture for chordal graphs and its restriction to split graphs, with counterexamples on eleven and fourteen vertices, respectively. For the score polytope P_G of the external bizonotopal algebra, we give a geometric realization of loopy deletion-contraction. The resulting forest-indexed geometric parking complexes partition the lattice points of P_G and are piecewise integral-affinely parametrized by boxes whose interval lengths are the component indices in the forest expansion.
item.dc:creator: Anatol Kirillov, Gleb Nenashev, Boris Shapiro, Arkady Vaintrob

item.title: Four Special Directions over Prime Fields: Structure and Complete Classification
item.description: arXiv:2609.20495v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A direction of the affine plane $\mathbb{F}_p^2$ is special for a set if the lines in that direction do not all meet the set in the same number of points. We classify, for every prime $p\ge5$, the subsets of $\mathbb{F}_p^2$ with exactly four special directions. There are $54$ affine-equivalence classes, occurring only for $p=5,7,11,13,17$, and we give explicit representatives. In particular, $17$ is the largest prime admitting such a set, which answers a question of Ghidelli, Kiss and Somlai, and over $\mathbb{F}_{13}$ the minimum size is $65$, attained by exactly two classes. The key structural fact is that the projection polynomials of such a set share a vertex: the set is either centrally symmetric about this point or differs from its reflection by exchanging one full line with one empty line. We also show that, over an odd prime field, a Boolean function on $\mathbb{F}_p^d$ with exactly four active projective Fourier lines is pulled back from a plane, so the classification extends to every dimension. The classification and the exclusion of the primes $19\le p<2048$ are computer-assisted; the structural results and the exclusion of larger primes are proved directly.
item.dc:creator: Qihang Wang

item.title: Wild frieze patterns over the integers
item.description: arXiv:2609.20967v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study frieze patterns over the integers that are allowed to have wild entries. We introduce the quiddity number as a new invariant. The quiddity number is then used to classify strongly connected components of the directed graph $\Gamma_{2,n}(\mathbb{Z})$. Furthermore, we show that every finite simple directed graph arises as an induced subgraph of a directed graph $\Gamma_{2,n}(\mathbb{Z})$ for $n$ sufficiently large.
item.dc:creator: Leon Eickhoff

item.title: Macdonald principal specialization ratios and their generating polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2609.21431v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish independence of $q$ as a necessary condition for coefficientwise nonnegativity of normalized principal specialization ratios of monic Macdonald polynomials. For arbitrary pairs of partitions, we characterize independence of $q$. For denominator partitions with largest and smallest parts differing by at least two, every ratio independent of $q$ is a power of $t$. We classify the nonnegative ratios under addition of maximal rows and columns of fixed height. For rows of length at least two, the classification is equivalent to rectangular complementation. For arbitrary initial partitions, the generating polynomials of successive row ratios at the smallest number of variables admissible for all stages have simple negative real zeros with lower bounds for the ratios of consecutive absolute zeros. We derive a reciprocity criterion, bounds for gamma coefficients, and the corresponding Jack limit. For generalized staircases, we determine shortest horizontal and conjugate vertical strip sequences and obtain terminating basic hypergeometric representations.
item.dc:creator: Tatsushi Shimazaki

item.title: Chromatic Extremal Thresholds and the Multipartite $K_4$-Free Problem
item.description: arXiv:2609.27503v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For positive integers $n,r,t$, let $\delta(n,r,t)$ denote the maximum possible minimum degree of a balanced $r$-partite graph with parts of size $n$ and chromatic number at most $t$. Lo, Treglown and Zhao established a general upper bound for this parameter and used it, together with explicit constructions, to determine the corresponding multipartite clique threshold up to an additive constant in a broad parameter range. I determine the chromatic parameter throughout the range $r=mt-a$, $m\ge2$, $t\ge3$, $2\le a\le \min\{m,t-1\}$. The answer differs from the Lo--Treglown--Zhao upper bound by at most one. I give an explicit arithmetic criterion deciding when this one-unit correction occurs. The proof reduces the problem to an integer matrix extremum. In the boundary case, equality forces the supports of all mixed rows to form a spanning star, after which the only remaining obstruction is a divisibility condition. Combining this formula with the Andrasfai--Erdos--Sos theorem sharpens the known equality range for $f(n,r,t+1)=\delta(n,r,t)$. In particular, for $t=3$ it removes the remaining size restrictions at $r=10$ and $r=13$. Together with the $r=7$ result in arXiv:2609.19177, the classical $r=4$ case, and the known congruence classes, this gives a formula for the multipartite $K_4$-free problem for every admissible $r\ge4$ and every $n\ge1$.
item.dc:creator: Yuuki Kasugai

item.title: Resilient forest universality in percolated dense graphs
item.description: arXiv:2609.27927v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Christoph, M\"uyesser and Wigderson recently asked whether an approximate form of the Erd\H{o}s-S\'os conjecture is robust under random edge deletions. We establish a density-sensitive transference theorem that converts global resilience for bounded-degree trees in sparse random graphs into resilient forest universality in arbitrary dense host graphs. More precisely, if $F$ is an $N$-vertex graph of edge density $\lambda$ bounded away from zero and $p\in[K/N,1]$, then, with probability $1-o(1)$ uniformly over the host and the percolation parameter, every subgraph obtained from $F_p$ by deleting at most an $\alpha$-fraction of its edges contains every bounded-degree forest on at most $((1-\alpha)\lambda-\xi)N$ vertices. Consequently, for every $c>0$, $L\ge1$, fixed $D$ and $\alpha<c$, every graph $F$ on at most $Ld$ vertices with average degree at least $d$ has the property that, after percolation at any rate $p\in[K/d,1]$ and any subsequent deletion of at most an $\alpha$-fraction of the surviving edges, the remaining graph is universal for all forests on at most $(1-c)d$ vertices and maximum degree at most $D$. This includes vertex-disjoint packings of any prescribed collection of bounded-degree trees of that total order. We further obtain forest-universality results for graphs whose connected components have vertex-cover number at most $Cd$, and for graphs that can be brought into this form by deleting sufficiently few edges on the $dn$-scale.
item.dc:creator: Mostafa Mirabi

item.title: A Hopf Algebraic Theory of the Quantum Magnusian
item.description: arXiv:2609.33587v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a Hopf-algebraic theory of graph coefficients arising in the quantum Magnus expansion. At the classical level, the expansion is governed by directed trees, whereas its quantum counterpart involves loop graphs, multiple edges, and several types of edge data. We introduce a contraction Hopf algebra of mixed quivers containing these diagrams and closed under contraction. On this algebra we define a character $e$ from normalized linear-extension data, directed-tadpole factors, and a prescription for undirected edges, and let $\omega$ be its convolution inverse. Our main result is a universal closed formula for the connected function $\omega_c$ on every finite mixed quiver, expressed as a finite sum over ordered set partitions of the vertices. We also construct a weighted vertex-splitting Hopf structure on the unlocalized mixed-quiver algebra, with convolution $\star_V$ and canonical edge-weight character $\zeta_V$, such that $\omega_c=\log_{\star_V}\zeta_V$. Compatibility of the two coproducts and an explicit identity between their characters explain this equality. We further prove that the two-vertex contraction identity, tadpole factorization, vanishing on disconnected graphs, and boundary data uniquely determine $\omega_c$. For acyclic quivers, the formula reduces to a permutation formula with coefficients depending only on descent numbers. We derive this formula independently from the quantum Magnus expansion using operator products and Wick contractions, showing that the physical graph coefficients are governed by the convolution structure of the contraction Hopf algebra. Further consequences include a refined quantum Murua formula and orientation-sum identities related to Tutte and chromatic polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Li Guo, Joon-Hwi Kim, Jung-Wook Kim, Sungsoo Kim, Sangmin Lee, Jian-Rong Li

item.title: Unbounded log-concavity breaks in independence polynomials of spherically symmetric trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.04172v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using a dioid algebraic structure, we show that there exist spherically symmetric trees $T(2^m 1^n)$ whose independence polynomials exhibit multiple breaks in log-concavity, a result established by estimating the asymptotic growth of the coefficients of these polynomials. Provided the parameter $n$ is a sufficiently large odd integer, the number of breaks is bounded below by the Jacobsthal numbers. This result affirmatively answers a question raised by F. Bencs [D. Galvin, Trees with non log-concave independent set sequences, arXiv 2502.10654.v2].
item.dc:creator: C\'esar Bautista-Ramos

item.title: Graphic additive bases and graph flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.07034v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The lattice-coset method of Alon, Buci\'c, and Davies gives real solutions with controlled coordinates. We combine it with integer rounding to prescribe outdegrees and flows from spanning-tree packing. For every integer $q\ge3$, $q$ edge-disjoint spanning trees suffice for every outdegree prescription modulo $q$ whose sum is compatible with the number of edges. The tree count is optimal even for simple graphs. A common interval theorem extends the argument to totally unimodular matrices; for graphs, its partition inequalities admit a sharp allowance of two. Fractional packing characterizes when every prescription has a strongly connected realization and gives circular-flow bounds. In particular, for every integer $k\ge1$, every $(4k+2)$-edge-connected graph has circular flow number strictly below $2+1/k$, with optimal connectivity for this strict inequality. As a structural application, every four-edge-connected graph with no bond of size six, seven or eight has a nowhere-zero three-flow. Further consequences concern star decompositions, antisymmetric flows and contraction.
item.dc:creator: Amir Jafari

item.title: On the number of cokernel-closed additive subcategories for uniformly oriented $A_n$ quivers
item.description: arXiv:2610.07999v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the integer sequence that enumerates cokernel-closed, idempotent split, full, additive subcategories of the category of finite dimensional complex representations of a uniformly oriented $A_n$ quiver. Using a combinatorial model, we describe a non-obvious connection of this sequence to Catalan numbers and derive an implicit recurrence. We also describe some basic properties of the lattice underlying the sequences, in particular, we give an explicit description of the meet irreducible elements of that lattice.
item.dc:creator: Volodymyr Mazorchuk, Shuoyang Xu

item.title: Positive Lin-Lu-Yau curvature, planar graphs, and forbidden minors
item.description: arXiv:2610.10307v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Over the past few decades, several notions of graph curvature have been introduced. Among them, Ollivier curvature, defined through optimal transport, and its Lin--Lu--Yau variant provide notions of curvature for graphs which retain several features of their counterpart in Riemannian geometry. A classical problem in this context is to understand the global structure of positively curved spaces. Lu and Wang proved that there are only finitely many positively curved planar graphs of minimum degree at least 3. In this paper, we study two directions motivated by this result. We first show that for fixed $2\leq s\leq t$, there are only finitely many positively curved $K_{s,t}$-minor-free graphs with minimum degree at least $s$. In particular, this generalizes the result of Lu and Wang to graphs embeddable on any fixed surface. We then give a complete classification of positively curved 5-connected plane triangulations. In particular, we show that there are only five examples, on 12, 14, 15, 16, and 17 vertices.
item.dc:creator: Louis Esperet, Julie Semaan

item.title: A rank bound for bases and circuits in binary matroids
item.description: arXiv:2610.11829v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let \(b(M)\), \(d(M)\), and \(r(M)\) denote the number of bases, the number of circuits, and the rank of a matroid \(M\), respectively. We prove that every nonempty simple binary matroid with no coloops satisfies \[ 2b(M)\ge(r(M)+1)d(M), \] with equality if and only if \(M\) is isomorphic to the Fano matroid.
