This confirms a conjecture recorded by Oxley in 1983. For the same class, we prove that deleting any element leaves at least as many bases as there are circuits in the original matroid: \(b(M\backslash e)\ge d(M)\) for every \(e\in E(M)\). We determine all equality cases and deduce a sharp linear lower bound for basis growth under successive series extensions. We also give a circuit-size exclusion condition guaranteeing distinct bases containing \(C-e\) for circuit-element pairs \((C,e)\) with prescribed circuit sizes.
item.dc:creator: Houshan Fu

item.title: Supersaturation thresholds for expanded color-critical graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.15348v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a $k$-uniform hypergraph $L$, let $h_L(n,q)$ be the minimum number of copies of $L$ in an $n$-vertex $k$-graph with $\mathrm{ex}(n,L)+q$ edges. Let $t_L(n,q)$ be the minimum number of copies obtained by adding $q$ edges to an extremal $L$-free $k$-graph. A graph is color-critical if deleting a suitable edge decreases its chromatic number. Let $\mathcal K_k(F)$ be the expanded graph obtained by adding $k-2$ new vertices to each edge of $F$, with disjoint sets of new vertices for distinct edges. Mubayi proved that, for every clique $K_r$ with $r\ge4$ and fixed $ q>0$, $ h_{\mathcal K_3(K_r)}(n,q)\ge qt_{\mathcal K_3(K_r)}(n,1)$ for every sufficiently large $n$. Pikhurko and Yilma later proved that, for every color-critical graph $F$, there is a constant $\epsilon_F>0$ such that $h_{F}(n,q)=t_{F}(n,q)$ for every sufficiently large $n$ and $1\le q\le\epsilon_F n$. We extend this equality to expanded color-critical graphs. Let $d>k\ge3$. For every color-critical graph $F$ with $\chi(F)=d+1$, there is a constant $\epsilon>0$ such that $ h_{\mathcal K_k(F)}(n,q)=t_{\mathcal K_k(F)}(n,q)$ for every sufficiently large $n$ and $1\le q\le\epsilon n^{k-1}$. Let $q_L(n)$ be the largest integer $q$ such that $h_L(n,s)=t_L(n,s)$ for every integer $1\le s\le q$. We give a sufficient condition for $q_L(n)=\Theta_L(n^{k-1})$ and an explicit family satisfying it. We also give a different sufficient condition under which $q_L(n)=\Omega_L(n^{k-1/2})$ and an explicit family satisfying it. \noindent \emph{Keywords.} Supersaturation; extremal graph; color-critical graph; chromatic number; expanded graph; hypergraph.
item.dc:creator: Liping Zhang, Qinghai Liu, Yanmei Hong, Wang Xi, Jinze Hu

item.title: Uniform Asymptotics for Andrews-Beck Partition Statistics
item.description: arXiv:2610.16024v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\NT(m,n)$ be the total number of parts in the partitions of $n$ with rank $m$, and let $\MW(m,n)$ be the total number of ones in the partitions of $n$ with crank $m$. Using the uniform generalized-rank estimate of Liu and Zhou, we establish asymptotic formulas for $NT(m,n)$ and $\MW(m,n)$. Put $\beta_n=\pi/\sqrt{6n}$ and $L_n=\log(1/\beta_n)$. For every fixed $A>0$, uniformly for $|m|\le A\sqrt n$, we prove \begin{align*} \NT(m,n)&=\frac{p(n)L_n}{4}\sech^2\!\left(\frac{\beta_nm}{2}\right) +O_A\!\bigl(p(n)\log L_n\bigr) \intertext{ and} \MW(m,n)&=\frac{p(n)}4\log(1+e^{-\beta_nm}) \sech^2\!\left(\frac{\beta_nm}{2}\right) +O_A\!\bigl(p(n)\sqrt{\beta_nL_n}\bigr). \end{align*}
item.dc:creator: Renrong Mao

item.title: Complete counterexamples to Mubayi's supersaturation conjecture for graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.18876v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a graph $F$, its extremal number ${\rm ex}(n,F)$ and extremal graphs denote the maximum number of edges in $F$-free graphs and the graphs attaining this maximum, respectively. Let $h_F(n,q)$ be the minimum number of copies of $F$ in an $n$-vertex graph with ${\rm ex}(n,F)+q$ edges, and let $t_F(n,q)$ denote the corresponding minimum obtained by adding $q$ edges to an extremal graph. Mubayi (2013) conjectured that for every non-$r$-partite stable $r$-uniform hypergraph $F$ with $r\ge 2$, $h_F(n,q)\ge q\cdot t_F(n,1)$ holds for all sufficiently large $n$ and all integers $q\ge 1$. In this paper, we prove that Mubayi's conjecture fails in a stronger sense. For every integer $d\ge 2$, we construct a family of non-$d$-partite stable graphs $F$ such that $h_F(n,q)< q\cdot t_F(n,1)$ for all $1\le q\le O\bigl(n^{4/ 3}\bigr)$. In particular, these examplesis completely refute Mubayi's conjecture. \noindent\emph{Key words}: extremal graph; supersaturation; chromatic number.
item.dc:creator: Liping Zhang, Qinghai Liu

item.title: Continuous Narayana Interpolations: Hankel Total Positivity and Log-Convexity Preservation
item.description: arXiv:2610.19548v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a continuous interpolation between the type $B$ and shifted type $A$ Narayana triangles. Using a direct Gegenbauer-moment proof and a continuant comparison criterion, we show that the row polynomials form a coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive sequence for every real $\theta\ge0$, including associated Jacobi tails. Their $\gamma$-expansion, real-rootedness and Stieltjes moment representation are explicit, as are the exact orders of vanishing and extreme coefficients of arbitrary Hankel minors. This confirms and strengthens Rodelet--Causse--Tevlin's log-convexity conjecture for super Narayana polynomials. We further extend Wang--Yang's total positivity of the type~$A$ and $B$ Narayana triangles and strict total positivity of the associated squares to every real $\theta>-1$, using P\'olya-frequency sequences and a gamma-product moment representation. We also prove that the continuous Narayana transformations preserve strong $t$-log-convexity for every $\theta\ge0$, and that every $d$-Hoggatt transformation has the same property for integers $d\ge1$. The preservation proofs employ the Zhu--Sun criterion and a mixed-minor one-sign-change argument based on a hypergeometric hitting-probability inequality. All results and proofs in this paper are classical.
item.dc:creator: Jiang Zeng

item.title: Cotangent cohomology and higher-order obstructions of matroids
item.description: arXiv:2610.20649v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Matroid Stanley-Reisner rings admit essential deformation obstructions of arbitrarily high order over every field, already at corank three. For each $m\ge3$, we construct a connected cosimple matroid and $m$ fine-homogeneous first-order classes whose proper subcollections integrate jointly and whose pairwise primary cup products vanish. A specified joint $(m-1)$-jet nevertheless has no lift to order $m$, even without preserving the grading. The construction rests on formulas for every multigraded component of the second cotangent cohomology $T^2$ and of its primary cup image, expressed through flats and parallel classes of the dual matroid. These formulas show that $T^2$ vanishes exactly when every connected component has corank at most two, or equivalently when there is no $U_{1,4}$-minor. This proves a conjecture of Constantinescu, Klein, Nguyen, Singh, and Venturello (2025) and characterizes formal smoothness of the affine deformation functor. For the duals of rank-three truncations of $U_{2,m}\oplus U_{2,n}$, $m,n\ge3$, each nonzero homogeneous class modulo the primary cup image is realized as a higher-order obstruction, and the quotient has an explicit presentation with $m+n-2$ minimal homogeneous generators.
item.dc:creator: Qihang Wang

item.title: Logical isomorphism and logical limit laws for small permutation classes and regular languages
item.description: arXiv:2610.22218v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we show that for each small permutation class $\mathcal{F}$ there exists a regular language $L_\mathcal{F}$ such that the monadic second-order TOTO logic on $\mathcal{F}$ is isomorphic to classical monadic second-order logic on $L_\mathcal{F}$. Thanks to the fact that regular languages are closed under monadic second-order restrictions this shows that many subsets of $\mathcal{F}$ have a well-behaved structure. In particular, this allows us to show that random permutations from any small permutation class satisfies convergence laws for both first-order logic and monadic second-order logic. In the latter case, the law is modular. Our proofs introduce a way of using the automaton description of regular languages to prove properties of generating functions which may be of independent interest. Potential applications include first-order limit laws for random words in some regular languages.
item.dc:creator: Klas Markstr\"om, Eero R\"aty

item.title: Semidefinite programming bounds for distance distribution of spherical codes
item.description: arXiv:2309.13854v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Multipoint semidefinite programming bounds for spherical codes use polynomials in several variables. We show how to obtain bounds for the distance distribution using a polynomial of one variable on a prescribed interval. The multivariate SDP supplies the required positivity; the sign and size of the univariate polynomial reveal the geometric consequences. We prove three- and four-point reductions and explain how to choose the polynomial to bound the number of pairs in a prescribed interval. Three-point experiments in dimension four illustrate this procedure, including nearly antipodal pairs, intervals near inner product $1/2$, and a local approach to the kissing number bound. As a further application, we extract a degree-six polynomial from the exact four-point construction of de Laat, Leijenhorst, and de Muinck Keizer. Its sign and four zeros give a direct description of the distance restriction underlying uniqueness of the $24$-cell.
item.dc:creator: Oleg R. Musin

item.title: Discrete $N$-particle systems at high temperature through Jack generating functions
item.description: arXiv:2502.13098v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We find necessary and sufficient conditions for the Law of Large Numbers for random discrete $N$-particle systems with the deformation (inverse temperature) parameter $\theta$, as their size $N$ tends to infinity simultaneously with the inverse temperature going to zero. Our conditions are expressed in terms of the Jack generating functions, and our analysis is based on the asymptotics of the action of Cherednik operators obtained via Hecke relations. We apply the general framework to obtain the LLN for a large class of Markov chains of $N$ nonintersecting particles with interaction of log-gas type, and the LLN for the multiplication of Jack polynomials, as the inverse temperature tends to zero. We express the answer in terms of novel one-parameter deformations of cumulants and their description provided by us recovers previous work by Bufetov--Gorin [Geom. Funct. Anal. 25 (2015), no. 3, 763-814] on quantized free cumulants when $\theta=1$, and by Benaych-Georges--Cuenca--Gorin [Comm. Math. Phys. 394 (2022), no. 2, 735-795] after a deformation to continuous space of random matrix eigenvalues. Our methods are robust enough to be applied to the fixed temperature regime, where we recover the LLN of Huang [Adv. Math. 380 (2021), Paper No. 107545, 91].
item.dc:creator: Cesar Cuenca, Maciej Do{\l}\k{e}ga

item.title: An Algebraic Approach to Periodicity and Complexity of Delone Sets
item.description: arXiv:2504.20709v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the connection between local complexity and periodicity of Delone sets using an algebraic approach based on annihilators, that is, finite linear relations between translations of a configuration. We model colored Delone sets (Delone multisets) as $\mathbb{R}^d$-configurations, that is, functions on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with finite range, and extend the notions of annihilators and periodizers from $\mathbb{Z}^d$-configurations to the geometric setting of Delone sets. Our main results describe the structure imposed by the existence of non-trivial annihilators. We show that any $\mathbb{R}^d$-configuration admitting non-trivial annihilators has an annihilator of a particularly simple form, namely a product of finitely many difference operators corresponding to translations in pairwise rationally independent directions. We further improve this result and prove that for configurations supported on Delone sets of finite local complexity (FLC), the corresponding directions can be chosen pairwise linearly independent over $\mathbb{R}$. As a consequence of the existence of the special annihilator, we show that $\mathbb{R}^d$-configurations with annihilators admit a decomposition into finitely many components that are periodic in pairwise rationally independent directions. Moreover, we connect local complexity with algebraic structure by proving that Meyer sets with sufficiently slow patch complexity growth have low pattern complexity and hence admit non-trivial annihilators. Finally, we establish a sufficient and necessary condition under which the existence of suitable annihilators forces periodicity of $\mathbb{R}^d$-configurations supported on FLC Delone sets.
item.dc:creator: Pyry Herva, Jarkko Kari

item.title: The Computational Complexity of Counting Linear Regions in ReLU Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2505.16716v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An established measure of the expressive power of a given ReLU neural network is the number of linear regions into which it partitions the input space. There exist many different, non-equivalent definitions of what a linear region actually is. We systematically assess which papers use which definitions and discuss how they relate to each other. We then analyze the computational complexity of counting the number of such regions for the various definitions. Generally, this turns out to be an intractable problem. We prove NP- and #P-hardness results already for networks with one hidden layer and strong hardness of approximation results for two or more hidden layers. Finally, on the algorithmic side, we demonstrate that counting linear regions can at least be achieved in polynomial space for some common definitions.
item.dc:creator: Moritz Stargalla, Christoph Hertrich, Daniel Reichman

item.title: Persistence probabilities for MA(1) sequences with uniform innovations
item.description: arXiv:2507.04427v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the persistence probabilities of a moving average process of order one with uniform innovations. We identify a number of regions-characterized by the location of the uniform distribution and the coupling parameter of the process-where the persistence probabilities have qualitatively different behaviour. We obtain the generating functions of the persistence probabilities explicitly in all possible regions. In some of the regions, the persistence probabilities can be expressed explicitly in terms of various combinatorial quantities.
item.dc:creator: Frank Aurzada, Kilian Raschel

item.title: Explicit computation of the generic degree of the generalized Verschiebung in rank two
item.description: arXiv:2509.03993v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to apply previous work on dormant opers to the study of the moduli space of stable bundles in positive characteristic. We affirmatively resolve the rank $2$ case of a conjecture proposed by the second author, which predicts a direct relationship between the number of higher-level dormant $\mathrm{PGL}_2$-opers and the generic degree of the generalized Verschiebung map for rank $2$ stable bundles induced by Frobenius pull-back. As a consequence, for a general smooth projective curve of genus $g>1$ in characteristic $p>2$, we obtain a procedure for explicitly determining these generic degrees by counting certain combinatorial objects and, in particular, compute $\mathrm{deg}(\mathrm{Ver}^2_1)$ as a polynomial in $p$ for $3\leq g\leq 10$.
item.dc:creator: Yuki Kondo, Yasuhiro Wakabayashi

item.title: Strict monotonicity of critical points in independent long-range percolation models
item.description: arXiv:2510.26314v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider independent long-range percolation models on locally finite vertex-transitive graphs. Using coupling ideas we prove strict monotonicity of the critical points with respect to local perturbations in the connection function, thereby improving upon previous results obtained via the classical essential enhancement method of Aizenman and Grimmett in several ways. In particular, our approach allows us to work under minimal assumptions, namely shift-invariance and summability of the connection function, and it applies to both undirected and directed bond percolation models.
item.dc:creator: Stein Andreas Bethuelsen, Christian M\"onch

item.title: A curiously slowly mixing Markov chain
item.description: arXiv:2511.01245v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a Markov chain with very different mixing rates depending on how mixing is measured. The chain is the "Burnside process on the hypercube $C_2^n$." Started at the all-zeros state, it mixes in a bounded number of steps, no matter how large $n$ is, in $\ell^1$ and in $\ell^2$. And started at general $x$, it mixes in at most $\log n$ steps in $\ell^1$. But, in $\ell^2$, it takes $\frac{n}{\log n}$ steps for most starting $x$. The $\ell^2$ mixing results follow from an explicit diagonalization of the Markov chain into binomial-coefficient-valued eigenvectors.
item.dc:creator: Persi Diaconis, Andrew Lin, Arun Ram

item.title: Improved exploration of temporal graphs
item.description: arXiv:2511.22604v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A temporal graph $G$ is a sequence $(G_t)_{t \in I}$ of graphs on the same vertex set of size $n$. The \emph{temporal exploration problem} asks for the length of the shortest sequence of vertices that starts at a given vertex, visits every vertex, and at each time step $t$ either stays at the current vertex or moves to an adjacent vertex in $G_t$. When each $G_t$ is connected and has bounded maximum degree, Erlebach, Kammer, Luo, Sajenko, and Spooner [ICALP 2019] showed that an exploration exists in $\mathcal{O}(n^{7/4})$ time steps. We significantly improve this bound by showing that $\mathcal{O}(n^{3/2}\sqrt{\log n})$ time steps suffice. In fact, we prove a more general statement unifying this setting with many others. Let the \emph{average temporal maximum degree} $D$ of $G$ be the average of $\max_{t \in I}d_{G_t}(v)$ over all vertices $v \in V(G)$, where $d_{G_t}(v)$ denotes the degree of $v$ in $G_t$. We show that if each $G_t$ is connected, then an exploration exists in $\mathcal{O}(n^{3/2}\sqrt{D\log n})$ time steps. This gives the first subquadratic upper bound when the underlying graph has bounded average degree, improving the previous best bounds when it is planar or has bounded treewidth. Our bound is subquadratic already when $D=o(n/\log n)$. In addition, we make progress on a recent conjecture of Baguley, G\"{o}bel, Klodt, Skretas, Sylvester, and Zamaraev [SODA 2025]. They conjectured that if $\mu$ is a probability distribution on trees with maximum degree at most $\Delta$ and each $G_t$ is sampled independently from $\mu$, then an exploration exists in $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{\Delta}n)$ time steps with high probability. We show that there is a temporal exploration of length $\mathcal{O}(\Delta n\log^3 n)$ with high probability. This improves the previous best bound of $\mathcal{O}(n^{3/2})$ and extends to the more general setup of average temporal maximum degree.
item.dc:creator: Paul Bastide, Carla Groenland, Lukas Michel, Cl\'ement Rambaud, Paulina Smolarova

item.title: Brion atoms for classical types
item.description: arXiv:2512.19034v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a classical group defined over the complex numbers with a Borel subgroup $B$. Choose a holomorphic involution of $G$ and let $K$ be its set of fixed points. The group $K$ acts on the flag variety $G/B$ with finitely many orbits and Brion has derived a general formula for the cohomology classes of the corresponding orbit closures as linear combinations of Schubert classes. This article provides a uniform description of the sets of Weyl group elements (which we refer to as Brion atoms) that index the terms in this formula. We also include some applications of our classifications, including a refinement of Brion's cohomology formula.
item.dc:creator: Eric Marberg

item.title: Schur--Weyl duality for diagonalizing a Markov chain on the hypercube
item.description: arXiv:2512.23285v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show how the tools of modern algebraic combinatorics -- representation theory, Murphy elements, and particularly Schur--Weyl duality -- can be used to give an explicit orthonormal basis of eigenfunctions for a "curiously slowly mixing Markov chain" on the space of binary $n$-tuples. The basis is used to give sharp rates of convergence to stationarity.
item.dc:creator: Persi Diaconis, Andrew Lin, Arun Ram

item.title: Combinatorial properties of holographic entropy inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2601.09987v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A holographic entropy inequality (HEI) is a linear inequality obeyed by Ryu-Takayanagi holographic entanglement entropies, or equivalently by the minimum cut function on weighted graphs. We establish a new combinatorial framework for studying HEIs, and use it to prove several properties they share, including two majorization-related properties as well as a necessary and sufficient condition for an inequality to be an HEI. We thereby resolve all the conjectures presented in [arXiv:2508.21823], proving two of them and disproving the other two. In particular, we show that the null reduction of any superbalanced HEI passes the majorization test defined in [arXiv:2508.21823], thereby providing strong new evidence that all HEIs are obeyed in time-dependent holographic states.
item.dc:creator: Guglielmo Grimaldi, Matthew Headrick, Veronika E. Hubeny, Pavel Shteyner

item.title: The Closure of LCD-to-GI Reductions via Generalized Inner Products
item.description: arXiv:2605.23120v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Permutation Equivalence Problem (PEP) for linear complementary dual (LCD) codes reduces to Graph Isomorphism (GI) through the orthogonal projector onto the code, but this requires a trivial hull. We ask whether the reduction extends when the standard inner product is replaced by a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form \(M\). We make precise what it means for \(M\) to yield a valid reduction to GI and prove that, for length \(n \geq 3\) and every field size, this holds if and only if \(M\) is permutation-invariant. The reduction then reaches, beyond LCD codes, a class of codes with one-dimensional hull: exactly those whose hull is spanned by a vector with nonzero coordinate sum. We count these codes exactly; for odd \(q\), asymptotically the method covers a fraction \(\prod_{i \geq 2}(1+q^{-i})^{-1}\) of all codes, \(1 + q^{-1}\) times the fraction of LCD codes. A polynomial-time reduction algorithm is given.
item.dc:creator: Keita Ishizuka

item.title: Tropical Circuits with Scalar Multiplication Gates
item.description: arXiv:2607.11540v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study tropical circuits with scalar multiplication gates, that is, algebraic circuits whose gates implement $\max$, $+$, or multiplication with a positive constant. For such circuits, we prove exponential size lower bounds for computing maximum weight directed spanning trees and maximum weight bipartite perfect matchings. As a corollary, we obtain an exponential size separation between monotone and non-monotone maxout neural networks, which generalize the popularly used ReLU neural networks. One conclusion from this is that neural network models with enforced convexity constraints, such as input-convex neural networks (ICNNs), sometimes need to be exponentially larger than their unrestricted counterparts in order to express the same functions.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Hertrich, Moritz Stargalla

item.title: M\"obius functions for pseudo-Levi subgroups in finite general linear and symplectic groups
item.description: arXiv:2607.12522v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we compute the M\"obius function on the poset of pseudo-Levi subgroups containing a fixed maximal torus of two families of finite groups, $GL_n(q)$ and $Sp_{2n}(q)$, for some natural number $n$ and a prime power $q$, where $q>2n+1$. For the general linear group, we consider arbitrary tori, but for symplectic groups, we restrict to tori corresponding to the bipartitions of $n$ into odd integers. Also, we assume $q$ is even for the case of symplectic groups. The M\"obius function for the set of pseudo-Levi subgroups of a finite group $G$ is important for an explicit evaluation of the formula expressing the decomposition of tensor products of characters, as proved in Theorem 2 of the paper ''Multiplicity of characters of finite reductive groups and Drinfeld doubles'' [arXiv:2512.01432].
item.dc:creator: Aritra Kundu

item.title: Geometric $(1+\varepsilon)$-Spanners with Few Crossings
item.description: arXiv:2607.25040v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For $n$ points in the plane and $\varepsilon>0$, we construct a $(1+\varepsilon)$-spanner with $O(n/\varepsilon)$ edges in which every edge has $\tilde{O}(1/\varepsilon^3)$ crossings, the total number of crossings is $\tilde{O}(n/\varepsilon^4)$, and the ratio between the lengths of any two crossing edges is $O(1/\varepsilon^2)$. Our spanner construction substantially improves on the previous upper bound for the number of crossings in a $(1+\varepsilon)$-spanner, and it is the first spanner construction that ensures $O(1)$ crossings per edge for any constant $\varepsilon>0$. In contrast, we construct $n$ points in the plane for which every $(1+\varepsilon)$-spanner has $\Omega(n/\varepsilon^3)$ crossings, $n$ points for which every $(1+\varepsilon)$-spanner has an edge with $\Omega(1/\varepsilon^{5/2})$ crossings, and 4 points for which every $(1+\varepsilon)$-spanner contains two crossing edges where one is $\Omega(1/\varepsilon)$ times longer than the other.
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luu, Csaba D. T\'oth

item.title: Online Discrepancy for Sub-Exponential Product Distributions via Regularization
item.description: arXiv:2608.10040v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study online discrepancy minimization for independent random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with independent coordinates. Our deterministic algorithms require no knowledge of the horizon, and their guarantees hold at every prescribed deterministic terminal time $T$. For unit-variance sub-exponential coordinates with $\psi_1$-norms at most $\sigma$, we obtain terminal discrepancy $O(\sigma^4\sqrt n)$ with failure probability $\exp(-\Omega(\sigma^3\sqrt n))$. Independently masking centered unit-variance marks from the same class with retention probability $k/n$ gives $O(\sigma^4\sqrt k)$ discrepancy with failure probability $\exp(-\Omega(\sigma^3\sqrt k))$ when $k\gtrsim\log^2(2n)$. The fourth-power dependence on $\sigma$ is necessary for these sub-exponential classes at the stated confidence levels. For standard Gaussian marks, we obtain $O(\sqrt k+\sqrt{\log(2n)})$ discrepancy with failure probability $\exp(-\Omega(\sqrt k+\sqrt{\log(2n)}))$. Both terms are necessary up to absolute constants for $T\ge n$. In particular, $k\gtrsim\log n$ is the optimal sparsity threshold for $O(\sqrt k)$ discrepancy. For centered unit-variance sub-Gaussian marks with any fixed $\psi_2$-norm bound $\sigma$, logarithmic sparsity suffices for $O(\sigma\sqrt{k\log(e+\sigma)})$ discrepancy with probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$. For a dimension-dependent family of unit-variance laws with rare activations, matching bounds determine the fixed-confidence online discrepancy order $\Theta(\sqrt n\log\log n)$ at sufficiently long prescribed horizons. Our dense result generalizes the Rademacher-input theorem of Bansal and Spencer (2020) and establishes the horizon-independent $O(\sqrt n)$ Gaussian terminal discrepancy scale anticipated by Gamarnik et al. (2022). The proofs combine regularization, global Fenchel estimates, coupled Lyapunov functions, and terminal moment recursions.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Wengiel

item.title: On the Log-submodularity for zonoids: from Mixed Volume inequalities to the Hypercube
item.description: arXiv:2608.14909v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In convex geometry, a number of inequalities for the volume of coordinate projections of convex bodies share a common structural property. We formalize them as inequalities of log-submodularity type, providing a definition that stems from the notion of a submodular function. The Loomis-Whitney inequality and some of its generalizations are the most prominent examples. Some inequalities of log-submodularity type are valid for zonoids but not for general convex bodies. They have a natural meaning in statistics and information theory. We propose a new inequality of log-submodularity type for zonoids. In dimension 3, our inequality is equivalent to the log-submodularity conjecture for zonoids formulated by Fradelizi, Madiman, Meyer, and Zvavitch, which is true in dimension $3$ and false in higher dimensions. In contrast, our inequality is true in every dimension. We reduce our inequality to copositivity of a special polynomial, which we call the hypercube polynomial. For 4-dimensional zonoids, we verify the copositivity of the respective hypercube polynomial algebraically by providing a sum-of-squares certificate. In every dimension, a proof of copositivity of the hypercube polynomial that uses probability theory and well-known matrix inequalities has been produced by LLMs and brought to our attention. We present a detailed and easy-to-read version of this proof.
item.dc:creator: Gennadiy Averkov, Katherina von Dichter, Ivan Soprunov

item.title: Polynomially larger deletion codes by linear hashing of substring counts
item.description: arXiv:2609.19493v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We reduce the leading redundancy coefficient for binary codes correcting any fixed number $t\ge2$ of deletions from $2t$ to $2t-1$. This is the first improvement to that coefficient since Levenshtein's 1965 bound. More generally, over every fixed alphabet of size $q\ge2$, codes of length $n$ correcting any combination of at most $t$ insertions, deletions and substitutions exist with redundancy $(2t-1)\log_q n+O_t(\log_q\log_q n)$. For two deletions, the upper-bound coefficient drops from $4$ to $3$, halving the gap to the lower-bound coefficient $2$. The leading coefficient $2t-1$ also holds for $t$ bounded substring edits, where both the removed and inserted strings have bounded length. The proof combines random binary linear hashing of substring counts with a two-colouring argument. A linear dependence among differences of substring-count vectors forces their local changes to overlap, and this overlap lowers the redundancy coefficient from $2t$ to $2t-1$. The result provides an edit-distance analogue of Varshamov's 1957 bound in the Hamming metric, both in the leading redundancy coefficient and in the role of linear independence in the proof.
item.dc:creator: Eyal En Gad

item.title: Chow Vanishing and Motives of Cluster Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2609.19744v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the integral Chow groups $CH_i$ and mixed Hodge degree $H^{2i, (i, i)}$ cohomology groups of a really full rank (RFR) sink-recurrent cluster variety vanish for $i > 0$. In particular this applies to braid varieties and open projected Richardson varieties in any Lie type. Our main technical tool is the construction of a stratification of any RFR sink-recurrent cluster variety $\mathcal{A}(\Sigma)$ over any field $k$ into (affine space times) RFR sink-recurrent cluster varieties of seeds with fewer mutable vertices than $\Sigma$, with which we show that RFR sink-recurrent cluster varieties are linear in the sense of Totaro. We also show that cycle class maps are isomorphisms onto the lowest-weight part of rational Borel-Moore homology for any mixed Tate variety over a number field. Finally, we use our results to deduce vanishing theorems for the Khovanov-Rozansky homology groups of closures of positive braids and generation properties for the Chow groups of flag Richardson, projected Richardson, and brick varieties: namely, that these groups are generated integrally by the fundamental classes of their closed Richardson, positroid, and braid strata, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Josephine Hlavinka

item.title: Exponential improvements in Rado's covering problem
item.description: arXiv:2609.25288v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $B^d$ denote the $d$-dimensional Euclidean ball of unit radius. What is the largest constant $f(B^d) \in [0,1]$ with the property that every finite collection $\mathcal{C}$ of unit balls in $\mathbb{R}^d$ admits a disjoint sub-collection $\mathcal{S}$ occupying at least a fraction $f(B^d)$ of the volume of $\mathcal{C}$? This problem was first raised by T. Rad\'o in 1928, for axis-parallel squares in the plane; the author was motivated by a classical covering lemma in real analysis due to Vitali. The case of Euclidean balls was first considered by R. Rado in 1949. Until last year the best known estimates on $f(B^d)$ for unit balls where very far apart: \[ (1+\epsilon_d) 3^{-d} \leq f(B^d) \leq 2^{-d}, \] where $0<\epsilon_d=o_{d\rightarrow \infty}(1)$. Recently, the authors of this note observed that an exponential improvement on the upper bound follows from the Kabatiansky--Levenshtein spherical code bound, while the lower bound was improved by a linear factor by C.~Xie and G.~Ge (see arxiv:2608.09744). The current best estimates for large $d$ are \[ c \cdot d \cdot 3^{-d} \leq f(B^d) \leq 2.447^{-d}, \] where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. Here we offer the first exponential improvement of the lower bound in almost 80 years, which narrows the gap to: \[ 2.910^{-d} \leq f(B^d) \leq 2.447^{-d}. \] Our method is constructive and yields a polynomial time algorithm for finding a disjoint sub-collection realizing the estimate. Moreover the same technique gives similar exponentially improved lower bounds for all symmetric convex bodies satisfying a uniform convexity assumption, e.g., $\ell^p$-balls for all $p\in (1,\infty)$.
item.dc:creator: Gian Maria Dall'Ara, Adrian Dumitrescu

item.title: Watkins's conjecture holds for all infinite groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.01049v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that at every infinite cardinality, every group which is neither abelian of exponent greater than two nor generalized dicyclic admits a graphical regular representation, settling the infinite-group part of Watkins's conjecture. We also determine the Cayley index of every infinite group: it is $1$, $2$, or $8$, according to its algebraic type, and in every case the index is attained by a connected Cayley graph. For every infinite group $G$ of cardinality $\kappa$, we construct $2^\kappa$ pairwise nonisomorphic Cayley graphs with exactly the unavoidable inverse-pair symmetries, diameter two, and $\kappa$ common neighbors at every distinct pair. The principal tool recovers a continuous ordinal hierarchy from an alternating adjacency baseline with bounded-degree errors: robust finite patterns identify the initial classes, successive twin quotients recover the layers, and their finite exception packets determine the translation action. The reconstruction applies without a group action and is stable under additional layerwise bounded-degree edits. Further results give closed Cantor-cube families with prescribed finite data in the regular cases, sharp cofinality-dependent graph properties, and optimal three-valued shortest-path metrics.
item.dc:creator: Alex J. Sutherland

item.title: Seed thresholds and degree variance in heterogeneous bootstrap percolation with growing degrees
item.description: arXiv:2610.04420v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study bootstrap percolation with independent vertex thresholds taking values one and two, with threshold-one probability $(1-c/d)/d$ for fixed $c>0$. The seed set is chosen uniformly among sets of a prescribed deterministic size, independently of the graph and thresholds. We prove threshold statements at fixed relative margins. For uniform simple graphs with prescribed nonnegative integer degrees of even sum and exact mean $d$, assume $\max_i|d_i-d|\le C\sqrt d$ and $c+1-v_n\ge\kappa>0$, where $v_n=\operatorname{Var}(D)/d$ and $C,\kappa$ are fixed. When $d\to\infty$ and $d=o(n^{1/7})$, the leading seed scale is $n(c+1-v_n)^2/(2d^4)$, without requiring a limit of $v_n$. At fixed relative margins below and above this scale, the final active set has size $O(n/d^3)$ and $n-o(n)$, respectively, with high probability. For regular graphs, the supercritical conclusion strengthens to full activation. For $G(n,d/n)$, the same $O(n/d^3)$ and $n-o(n)$ conclusions hold when $d\to\infty$ and $d^5/n\to0$, with seed scale $nc^2/(2d^4)$. Thus regular and independent-edge graphs have different coefficients at the same asymptotic mean degree. Local exploration estimates yield explicit inactive remainders and survive conditioning on simplicity in the prescribed model. We also quantify the precision obstruction to static inclusion transfer and compute deterministic response-barrier corrections, without identifying a shrinking random critical window.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandr Rodionov

item.title: Biquandle-Based Invariants of Virtual Knotoids and Connected Sum
item.description: arXiv:2610.07187v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the behavior of biquandle-based invariants of virtual knotoids under their connected sum. We first show that the fundamental biquandle of the connected sum of two virtual knotoids is the pushout of a span in the category of biquandles. By applying the Hom functor to this pushout description, we obtain the correspondence between biquandle colorings of $K_1 \# K_2$ and compatible pairs of colorings of summands. This provides a categorical explanation of a known matrix product formula for biquandle counting matrices under connected sum. We then study the behavior of biquandle virtual bracket invariants under connected sum. We introduce normalized multiset invariants derived from biquandle virtual brackets and show that they are strictly stronger than their unnormalized versions in certain cases by an explicit example. Furthermore, we show that for each coloring of the connected sum $K_1 \# K_2$ corresponding to a compatible pair of colorings of the summands $K_1$ and $K_2$, the normalized biquandle virtual bracket value factors as the product of the normalized values of the summands. Building on this, we obtain connected-sum formulas for the normalized multiset invariants defined by utilizing biquandle virtual brackets. When the coefficient ring is a number ring, the normalized bracket multisets can be encoded by polynomials and matrices with polynomial entries. We introduce an induced matrix product $\odot$ and show that the normalized biquandle virtual bracket matrices satisfy \begin{equation} \widetilde{M}_X^\beta(K_1 \# K_2) = \widetilde{M}_X^\beta(K_1) \odot \widetilde{M}_X^\beta(K_2). \end{equation}
item.dc:creator: Hamdi Kayaslan, Sel\c{c}uk \.Ilbeyli

item.title: Comparing word probabilities in finite groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.23100v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We use results from extremal graph theory and analysis to compare word probabilities in finite groups. In particular, we show that the probability of satisfying the 2-Engel word admits a positive lower bound in terms of the probability that an element has order dividing 3. More generally, using a group removal lemma, we obtain analogous bounds for $x^m$-good words.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Putignano, Matteo Vannacci
